paragraphs.text: IV. That Those Who Sin Against God Are Not to Be Spared

Emperor, when you saw yourself beaten on every side by the servants of God, you said that you had suffered, and are still suffering, insult from us against the warnings of the sacred Scriptures. You say that we have been insolent toward you, whom we ought to have honored. If any worshipper of God has ever spared apostates, then let what you say about us be true. Where shall we begin, so that we can prove that every one who strayed has been rebuked by the worshippers of God, just as you are now rebuked by us? Where else but with the acts of Moses, the servant of God? We read in Exodus that after the covenant had been handed to him, Moses went up the mountain and killed a great many of them for the guilt of idolatry. "Moses stood at the gate of the camp," it says, "and said: Who is ready for the Lord? Let him come to me. And all the sons of Levi gathered to him, and he said to them: Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Let every man put his sword on his thigh, and go through the camp and back from gate to gate, and let every man kill his brother, and every man his kinsman, and every man his neighbour. And the sons of Levi did as Moses told them. And about three thousand men of the people fell that day. And Moses said to them: Today you have filled your hands for the Lord, each of you against his son or his brother, so that a blessing may be given among you." We are as insulting to you as Moses was to that foolish people. They did not like what Moses said or did either, since they had already chosen to serve, not the God who had rescued them from Pharaoh's power, but the calf that the fire had cast for them. In the same way you, now bound over not to God but to the idolatry of Arius, resent being shown to be in error. You keep crying out that we are defiant. You say that we have committed a shameful crime against you, because we dared to say to the emperor of the Roman realm: "You do wrong, Constantius, to bring idolatry into the Church." Moses, the first of the prophets and most beloved of God, pursued with the sword the very people you have made yourself an imitator of. Am I then to be branded defiant by you because I said that God has forsaken you and that you have bound yourself over to idolatry? Holy Scripture also proclaims that the sons of Israel committed fornication with the daughters of the Moabites, and that when the women invited them they ate things sacrificed to idols and worshipped those same idols. The priest Phinehas, set on fire with the zeal of devotion, blazed out against them, and above all he killed the idolaters with the sword in the middle of the assembly. For this he so pleased God that it is written that at this deed the wrath of the angry Lord was stilled and Phinehas himself became exceedingly eminent before the Lord: "And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, has turned back my wrath from the sons of Israel, in that he was zealous with zeal among them, and I did not consume the sons of Israel in my zeal. And behold, I will give him my covenant, a covenant of peace, to him and to his seed with him, as a covenant of everlasting priesthood, because he was zealous for his God and made atonement for the sons of Israel." And do you think us defiant because we tell you the truth while you are in error? Do you suppose that when we displease you, we are not pleasing God? But tell me, I beg you, Constantius: by what authority did you want us to abandon the way of the righteous patriarchs, prophets, apostles and martyrs and take up this new way of yours, which the devil had set up through Arius? Were you warned in a dream? Were you told not to allow us to hold to the way of Christ? That was the way held by Abel, Enoch, Noah, Melchizedek, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, Joseph, Moses, Aaron, Joshua son of Nun, Job, the judges and the other kings, that is, David, Jehoshaphat, Hezekiah and Josiah. It was held by all the prophets, apostles and martyrs, and by all who are found to have pleased God.

If the prince of demons told you this, hear what God has decreed, through the glorious prophet Moses, should be done to you: "If a prophet arises among you, or a dreamer of dreams, and gives a sign or a wonder, and comes performing signs or wonders, and says to you: Let us go and serve foreign gods whom you do not know, you shall not listen to the word of that prophet or dreamer, for the Lord your God is testing you, to see whether you love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul. You shall walk after the Lord your God and fear him, keep his commandments and hear his voice, and you shall cling to him. And that prophet or dreamer of dreams shall be put to death, for they have spoken to lead you astray from the Lord your God." Do you see what you have been ordered to suffer? Whether you say that you were warned in a dream or want to present yourself to us as a prophet, you are an enemy of God, since you want us to abandon the apostolic faith and take up one that denies the only Son of God. It is clear that all those I have named became so great and so excellent because they believed in the only Son of God. For whoever does not believe in the Son does not have the Father either, but whoever believes in the Son has both the Father and the Son. These are the words of blessed John, and the whole choir of holy apostles is at one with him. You must therefore understand that the patriarchs and prophets believed beforehand just as the apostles believed, and so did all who are known to have been honoured for the merit of their faith. You will not be able to prove to me that Abraham, Isaac and Jacob believed one thing, and John and all his fellow apostles another. If the apostles did not believe as the patriarchs believed, why does blessed Paul call everyone to lay hold of the faith of Abraham? But you say: "I am rebuking you for being insolent and for insulting the emperor, and you go back over the question of the faith." Yes, of the faith, so that I may prove that you are sacrilegious and that you have strayed from the way of truth. That is why I seem insulting to you: because I tell you that you have abandoned the path of all who worship God and taken up the one held, then and now, by those who served and still serve not God but a phantom. So, since you urge me to depart from God, hear what God decreed through Moses should be done about you: "If your brother, the son of your father or of your mother, or your son, or your daughter, or the wife in your bosom, or the friend who is as dear as your own soul, entices you secretly, saying: Let us go and serve foreign gods, which neither you nor your fathers have known, gods of the nations around you, near or far, do not agree to go with him and do not listen to him. Your eye shall not spare him, you shall not greet him, and you shall not hide him. You shall surely report him. Your hands shall be the first upon him to put him to death, and afterwards the hands of your people. And you shall stone him, and he shall die, because he sought to turn you away from the Lord your God." You do not know that you, who invite me to forsake God, are commanded to be killed, and so you say: "Lucifer insults me." Or will you deny that you invited us to take up idolatry? If you think you should deny it, the doctrinal statements of the bishops of your sect, your fellow blasphemers, will convict you. So will the pamphlets you had read out and handed to bishops at Rome, even catholic ones, for the express purpose of strengthening your blasphemy everywhere.

Do you not perceive the darkness of error you have run into? Do you not see how you may perish? Achan, one of the people, acted against the divine commands and stole a share of clothing, silver and gold from Jericho, and for this he was punished with death. When you see that, consider what will happen to you, who deny the eternal divine majesty of the only Son of God. Hear what was done in Achan's case, and at last look to your salvation. Return to the Church of God, from which, through the Arians, you have been driven by that renegade serpent who also overthrew Adam and Eve. "And the Lord was with Joshua," it says, "and his name was over all the earth. But the sons of Israel committed a great trespass and acted fraudulently concerning the accursed thing. And the Lord was angry with the sons of Israel. And Joshua sent men to Ai, which is next to Bethel, saying: Spy out Ai. And the men went up and spied out Ai. And they returned to Joshua and said to him: Let not all the people go up, but let about two or three thousand men go up and lay waste the city. Do not lead all the people there, for the enemy are few. And about three thousand men went up there, and they fled before the men of Ai. And the men of Ai killed thirty-six of them, and pursued them from the gate and crushed them on the slope; and the heart of the people was afraid and became like water. And Joshua tore his clothes and fell on his face before God until evening, he and the elders of Israel, and they put dust on their heads. And Joshua said: I pray you, Lord, why did your servant bring this people across the Jordan, to hand it over to the Amorite and destroy us? If only we had stayed in the land, we would have settled beside the Jordan. And what shall I say, now that Israel has turned its back before its enemy? The Canaanite and all who live in the land will hear of it, and they will surround us and wipe us from the earth. And what will you do for your great name? And the Lord said to Joshua: Get up; why have you fallen on your face? The people have sinned and broken my covenant which I made with them; they have stolen from the accursed thing and put it among their own goods. The sons of Israel will not be able to stand against their enemies; they will turn their backs before their enemies, because they have become accursed. I will be with you no longer unless you remove the accursed thing from among you. Get up, sanctify the people and say: Sanctify yourselves for tomorrow. For thus says the Lord God of Israel: There is an accursed thing among you; you will not be able to stand against your enemies until you remove the accursed thing from among you. Assemble in the morning, all of you, by tribes; and the tribe that God points out in the morning, bring forward by clans; the clan that the Lord points out, bring forward man by man; and whoever the Lord points out shall be burned with fire, with all that is his, because he has broken the covenant of the Lord and done wickedness in Israel. And Joshua rose early in the morning and brought the people forward by tribes, and the tribe of Judah was pointed out. And they were brought forward by clans, and the clan of Zerah was pointed out. And he brought the clan of Zerah forward by households, and the household of Zabdi was pointed out. And the household was brought forward man by man, and Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, was pointed out. And Joshua said to Achan: Give glory today to the Lord God of Israel, and make confession, and tell me what you have done, and do not hide it from me. And Achan answered Joshua and said: Truly I have sinned before the Lord God of Israel; this and this is what I did. I saw among the spoil a fine embroidered garment, two hundred didrachms of silver and a bar of gold weighing fifty didrachms, and I coveted them and took them; and look, they are hidden in my tent, with the silver hidden underneath. And Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent, and the things were hidden in the tent with the silver underneath. And they took them out of the tent and brought them to Joshua and the elders of Israel and laid them before the Lord. And they seized Achan son of Carmi and led into the valley [?] Achan and his sons and daughters, his calves, his yoke-animals, his sheep, his tent and everything that was his. And all Israel was with him, and they led them to Emek-achor. And Joshua said to Achan: Why have you destroyed us? May the Lord destroy you this day. And all Israel stoned him with stones and raised a great heap of stones over him. And the Lord turned from his fierce anger." Consider, Constantius, after what example you are going to perish, and what penalties you will pay for eternity, unless you look out for yourself. Achan suffered such things for breaking the commandments; from this one may understand what you deserve, since you are an apostate. If he was punished with such destruction for having some of the accursed thing, how much more will you be! Without a doubt you will be punished more severely, for you have made yourself accursed by denying the Son of God.

This is why you think us wicked, proud, obstinate and insolent: because we say to you, "You have committed sacrilege by denying the only Son of God," and because we say, "Look to yourself; rescue your soul from the snares of the devil." What new thing are we bishops doing if we tell you what you deserve to hear? We find that the most holy Samuel, the priest of God, said to King Saul the words you are about to read: "Pains and groans will be brought upon you. Because you have treated the word of the Lord as worthless, the Lord will treat you as worthless, so that you shall not reign." And again: "Since you have treated the word of the Lord as worthless, God will bring you to nothing, so that you shall not be king over Israel." And further on: "The Lord will tear the kingdom of Israel from your hand today and give it to your neighbour, who is better than you." If Samuel said these things to Saul because he had disregarded the Lord's commands, why do you think we should not have said openly that you are sacrilegious, and that unless you turn to God he will bring you to nothing? If we had not exhorted you, if we were not calling you to make amends, you could rightly say that we hate you. But when you hear us say, "Repent, emperor, correct your ways, so that you may find room for mercy," you ought, I think, to have considered that we in fact love you and hold you dear. Yet you curse us for this, for remaining in the apostolic faith; you repay good with evil. We are not surprised that you repay with evil those who pray God that it may go well with you and who wish it. You have departed from the will of God and never cease to do what the devil desires; doing evil is ingrained in you, for you have passed over from good to evil, that is, to the devil. If you persecute us, though we love you and wish every highest blessing to come to you, that is nothing great or new, since Saul too persecuted Samuel, the prophet and priest of the Lord. He persecuted the man who had anointed him king and whose prayers rose to the Lord in ceaseless supplication for the safety of this very persecutor. If you do not believe us when we say that we priests of God grieve for you, because you have drunk in so much darkness of error and are thus slaughtering yourself, then believe God, who said to Samuel about Saul: "How long will you mourn for Saul? Behold, I am driving him out, so that he shall not reign over Israel." And earlier: "And the word of the Lord came to Samuel, saying: I repent that I made Saul king, for he has turned away from me and has not carried out my words. And Samuel was grieved, and he cried to the Lord all night until before dawn." Although Samuel the priest did these things for King Saul's welfare, Saul later persecuted Samuel; the wretch did not realize that he was persecuting a prophet and priest of the Lord. In the same way you, not knowing what you are doing, persecute us, who long for you to please God, and you love those who are dragging you with them to eternal death and to the Lord's everlasting displeasure. You are indignant at hearing the truth, though you see that Samuel, the priest of the Lord, did not flatter the king. Or was it right for our predecessors to act one way and for us to act another? Because we tell you the truth, we seem proud to you. What have you heard from us? Only that you are a murderer. If we are lying, then you are right to call us insulting and proud. But if what we say is true, we are not insulting. We are imitating those who earned God's deepest love by not flattering those entrusted to them, but warning them in time for their salvation. When the king of Israel sent men to kill the prophet Elisha, Elisha said to those who were with him, "Do you see that this son of a murderer has sent to take off my head?" If you had not read that, you might rightly accuse me of slander. The prophet, full of the Holy Spirit, called the king of Israel the son of a murderer, that is, the son of the devil. He did not mean that the king's father in the flesh was a murderer; he meant the devil. Just as you now show by your deeds whose son you are, so that king showed himself to be the devil's son by persecuting the servants of God and daring to kill the prophets of the merciful God. It is the devil who stirs up your hearts to do all these things. To see that this is so, hear the Lord saying to the Jews in the Gospel: "You are born of the devil as your father, and you want to carry out your father's desires; for he was a murderer from the beginning." The prophet of the Lord, I say, full of the Holy Spirit, calls the king of Israel the son of a murderer, that is, of the devil. And do you think we insult you when we say that you kill the servants of God, butcher our bodies, have injustice in your every thought, destroy religion and deny the only Son of God? What we see you doing, we say you do; what you are, we proclaim you to be. You call us insolent because we tell you what you are.

Tell me, please: how did the king of Israel deserve to hear such words from the Lord as these: “Because you have done good in my sight and have done to the house of Ahab according to my heart and according to my soul, your sons to the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel”? Tell me, I say, why he deserved to hear this from God. Because he spared God's enemies? Or because he pursued them as fiercely as he could, even with the sword? Or because he killed the son of Ahab, an idolater, and his forty sons, and because he had Queen Jezebel killed and thrown to the dogs, and destroyed all the servants of Baal, with all the priests and prophets of shame, by the edge of the sword, and because he tore down the idols, he is pleasing to God? What, then, was it right for us to do about you, so that you would not brand us as guilty of insulting you, when we see you walking in the ways of Ahab and Jezebel? It is nothing new, what you are doing: acting against God, attacking his house, persecuting his bishops, the very men through whom he warns you to look to your own good and, while there is still room for repentance, to drag yourself away from evil. Before you there were others like you in sacrilege, who likewise served idols and abandoned the God of their fathers. In the second book of Chronicles we hear that Amaziah, king of Judah, was warned by God through a prophet not to let the men of Israel, whom he had hired for a hundred thousand talents of silver, go out with him to war, because God had abandoned Israel, since they had abandoned God and served idols. The king obeyed the prophet's words and believed that this was God's warning. And then what does he do? After he subdues his enemies, he decides that he should take their idols, bring them back to his own kingdom and even worship them; and because the man of God told him he had not done well in abandoning God to worship the idols of the nations, this king fiercely persecuted the Lord's prophet. You see that among you who have turned to apostasy there has always been one and the same mind: to persecute those who wish you well. “And it came to pass,” says holy Scripture, “after Amaziah came to strike Edom, that he brought from there the gods of Mount Seir and set them up as gods for himself, and he worshipped before them and sacrificed to them himself. And the wrath of the Lord came upon Amaziah, and he sent to him the prophet Baneas, and Baneas said to him: ‘Why have you sought the gods of a people that did not deliver their own people from your hand?’ And as he was speaking to him, the king said to him: ‘Have I made you the king's counselor? Take care that you are not flogged.’” You see, Constantius, how mad you all become once you have chosen to live in the service of the devil, once you have chosen not to know God almighty, once you have decided that you must set up idolatry as an insult to God. For as that king said, “Have I made you the king's counselor? Take care that you are not flogged,” so you too say: “Have I chosen you as my counselors, so that I may not act as I please, so that I may not keep to the way Arius kept to?” And do you not see by what kind of death Arius perished, how vengeance was taken on him by God? Meanwhile, since you say we insult you, see how this man of God did not spare that king, your fellow in sacrilege, but after he was told, “Be silent, or you will be flogged,” he said to him: “I know that the Lord will destroy you, because you have done this and have not listened to my counsel.” In what do you find us insulting? Surely in this, that we say to you: we know that unless you see to it that you turn to God, the Lord will condemn you to eternal punishment. This is the insult, this the whole injury: that God's bishops tell you that you will perish forever unless you correct your ways. That king did not believe the man of God. What happened to him at once, holy Scripture tells as follows: “And from the time that Amaziah turned away from the Lord, they rose up against him [?]. And he fled from Jerusalem to Lachish, and they killed him [?] on horses.” So too the deeds of your wicked companions will be able to preserve, protect and defend you, just as they did that man who said to the man of God when he spoke for his salvation: “Have I appointed you counselor to the king? Be silent, or you will be flogged.” We are not the first to do this, if we say to you, who are going astray, resisting God's ordinance and laboring to establish new ways: you do wrong not to walk on the way by which all the worshippers of God have reached the heavenly kingdom.

You have read that King Uzziah was rebuked by the priests of the Lord because he had dared to do what was unlawful. “And he went into the temple of the Lord,” says Scripture, “to burn incense on the altar. And Azariah the priest went in after him, and with him thirty priests of the Lord, men of valor, and they stood up against King Uzziah and said to him: ‘It is not lawful for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to the Lord, but for the priests, the sons of Aaron, who are consecrated to burn incense. Go out of the sanctuary, for you have departed from the Lord, and this will bring you no honor from the Lord God.’” Tell me, were the priests of the Lord insulting to that king or not? If they were not insulting, then neither should we seem so to you, since you hear from us much the same as he heard: It is not lawful for you, Constantius, an Arian, to assemble with God's people; it is not lawful for you, a promoter of the idolatry of the Arian heresy, a denier of the only Son of God, to sit in judgment on God's priests—you, a man of sacrilege pretending to be a Christian, when you are the forerunner of Antichrist. It will not go well for you that you remove God's priests and ordain his enemies, your companions in sacrilege, of course. When you hear this, you are angry with us; King Uzziah too was angry with those priests of the Lord in his day. But notice that those men consecrated to God kept the honor of their station forever, while Uzziah was at once marked with the blotches of leprosy, to his everlasting disgrace. “And Uzziah was angry,” it says, “and in his hand was the censer to burn incense on the altar. And leprosy appeared on his forehead before the priests in the house of the Lord.” Since this is so, do you suppose that you, a stubborn transgressor, do not incur the displeasure of him who commanded us to carry out forever the duties of the priesthood for his glory? What is this pride of ours, Constantius, what is this arrogance? Unless it is that we see you are diseased and pestilent, being an Arian; that we perceive in you the leprosy which Arius had; that we urge you to withdraw from the people of God, just as those priests of the Lord forced Uzziah to leave the temple; that in this way we compel you to give honor to God. For if God's priests drove Uzziah out of God's court because they remembered the divine command that lepers were forbidden to enter the temple before their cleansing, consider how much more right we have to drive you out of the church of Christ, out of the house of the Lord, since it is not lawful for a heretic to assemble with Catholics, the insane with the sane, one full of unclean spirits with those in whom the Spirit of God dwells. What insult is it if we, priests of the Lord, fired by the same zeal that always fired our predecessors, tell you what serves both our salvation and yours? “Lucifer is insolent,” you say. Insolent, then, because I urge you to cast off the leprosy of Arius, so that through this faith which the most blessed apostles preached, and which, as you see, we hold, you may obtain health for your mind and, wholly snatched from the snares of the devil, may rejoice forever at having been won for God. You who accuse us of overweening arrogance, you have found it written what Josiah, king of Judah, did to your fellows in sacrilege, men such as you are seen to be today: how he persecuted a great many of them even after death, burning their bones in the fire. But it was fitting for that king to persecute God's enemies with such zeal, while for us bishops, for us priests of God, it was unworthy to resist you as you bring idolatry into the church! He killed your fellows in sacrilege with the sword, and even persecuted remains long since buried, desiring to be found a most faithful worshipper of God; we, on the other hand, ought not to have resisted you even with a word—you, the friend of God's enemy, you, dearest of all to the angels who turned to apostasy, you who through this blasphemy of yours have become God's enemy.

Hear, then, in the fourth book of Kings what Josiah, servant of the Lord and king of Judah, gained because of what he did to your fellows in uncleanness, and stop at last saying of us, “They are proud and insulting.” “He did,” it says, “what was right in the sight of the Lord, and walked in the way of his father David, and did not turn aside to the right or to the left.” And again further on, after he had rebuilt the house of the Lord and the priest had sent the book of the law to the king: “And it came to pass, when the king heard the words of the book of the law, that he tore his clothes. And the king commanded Hilkiah the priest, and Alchina son of Josaphan, and Achilia son of Melchias, and Shaphan the scribe, and Joas the king's son, saying: ‘Inquire of the Lord for me and for all Judah concerning the words of this book that has been found, for great is the wrath of the Lord that is kindled against us, because our fathers did not listen to the words of this book, to do according to all that is written.’ And Hilkiah the priest and Acican and Shaphan and Joas went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Selle son of Tacuelas, keeper of the wardrobe; she lived in Jerusalem. And they spoke to her accordingly. And she said to them: ‘Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Say to the man who sent you to me: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will bring evils upon this place and upon those who live in it, according to all the words of this book which the king of Judah has read, because they have forsaken me and turned to foreign gods and provoked me with the works of their hands. And my wrath is kindled against this place and will not be quenched. And to the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of the Lord, you shall say this: Thus says the Lord God of Israel: As for the words you have heard, because you revered my presence when you heard what I spoke against this place and those who live in it, that they would become a wilderness and a curse, and you tore your clothes and wept before me, I too have heard, says the Lord of hosts. Therefore I will gather you to your fathers, and you will be added to them in peace, and your eyes will see all the evils which I am bringing upon this place and upon those who live in it.’ And they brought back word to the king, and King Josiah sent and gathered to himself all the elders of Judah in Jerusalem. And the king went up to the Lord, and all the men of Judah, and the priests and the Levites, and all the people, from the least to the greatest. And the king read in the hearing of the people all the words of the book of the covenant which had been found in the house of the Lord. And the king stood by the pillar and made the covenant that had been found in the house of the Lord, before the Lord, to walk after the Lord and to keep his commandments and his testimonies and his precepts with all his heart and all his soul, to establish all the words of this covenant written in this book. And all the people entered into the covenant which the king had made from the book. And the king commanded Hilkiah the high priest and the priests of the second rank and the keepers of the ephod to cast out of the house of the Lord all the vessels made for Baal and Asherah and for all the host of heaven. And he burned them outside Jerusalem in the burning-place of the brook Kidron, and took their ashes and scattered them in the brook, and went to Bethel. And he burned the priests whom the kings of Judah had appointed to burn incense on the high places in the cities of Judah and around Jerusalem; they burned incense to Baal and to the sun and the moon and all the host of heaven. And they brought it out of the house of the Lord, outside Jerusalem, to the brook Kidron, and he ground the ashes fine and threw them on the graves of the common people. And he dragged out their sons who were in the house of the Lord, whose women served there making robes. And he brought in all the priests from the cities of Judah and defiled the sanctuaries where the priests burned incense, from Geba to Beersheba, and he tore down their high places.” And further on: “And he defiled Phem [?], which was in Cepenan [?], because each of them had made his son and his daughter pass through the fire of Moloch. [?] which the kings of Judah had set up to the sun, from the entrance of the house of the Lord to [?] of the shepherds, which he set up [?] three horses, which were in Pharurim [?]; and he burned the fountain [?] of the sun with fire, in the house which the kings of Israel had built for that high place of Baal and for all the host of heaven. And there were altars on top of the upper buildings of Ahaz, which the king of Judah had made, and the altars which Manasseh made in the two courts of the house of the Lord; the king tore them down and removed them from there and threw their ashes into the brook Kidron. And the high places that they had made facing Jerusalem, which was on the right of the mount of Amissa [?], which King Solomon had built for Astarte, the idol of the Sidonians, and for Chemosh the idol, and for Milcom, the idol of the Ammonites, the king defiled. And he broke the pillars in pieces and filled their places with human bones. And the altar at Bethel, the high place which Jeroboam son of Nebat made, by which he made Israel sin—that altar and high place he tore down, and broke its stones in pieces and ground them to dust, and burned their groves. And King Josiah turned and saw the tombs that were there on the mountain, and he took the bones out of the tombs and burned them on the altar and defiled it, according to the word which the man of God spoke when Jeroboam was standing at the altar on the feast day.” What do you learn, Constantius, of what was done by a king who worshipped God? And because we strike you with a word as you bring idolatry into the church, you say, “Lucifer insults me”? When, had you been a man of that time, you could have been put to death by the sword, or had you already been dead, even your bones, as a man of sacrilege, would have been brought to nothing in the fire! He strikes those guilty of so great a crime with the sword, and we ought not even to wound you with a word? Notice meanwhile that here too those kings, your fellows in sacrilege, brought into the city of God, into the house of the Lord and into his temple, the idolatry which this King Josiah, wholly devoted to God, wiped out; and do not imagine that you are the only one who has undertaken this work against God. So I do not want you to say, “If I were acting wrongly, God would already have taken vengeance on me”; rather, I beg you to see that you are held captive by the devil and live under his power, just as those kings did whose works King Josiah pursued.

Because we curse your blasphemies, because we resist your wicked conspiracies, we seem to you to be abusive. So too the most holy prophets and the most blessed apostles seemed insulting and proud to the Jews, whom you imitate. In the book of the prophet Amos: “And Amaziah, the priest at Bethel, sent to Jeroboam, king of Israel, saying: ‘Amos is conspiring against you in the midst of the house of Israel; the land cannot bear his words. For this is what Amos says: Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall be led away captive from its land.’ And Amaziah said to Amos: ‘Go, depart to the land of Judah, and live there, and prophesy there. But at Bethel you shall prophesy no more, for it is the king's sanctuary and will be the house of the kingdom.’ And Amos answered and said to Amaziah: ‘I was no prophet, nor am I a prophet's son, but I was a goatherd and a gatherer [?], and the Lord took me from the flock and said to me: Go, prophesy to my people Israel. Now therefore hear the word of the Lord. You say: You shall not prophesy in Israel, and there shall be no gathering in the house of Jacob. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Your wife shall be a prostitute in the city, and your sons and your daughters shall fall by the sword, your land shall be measured out with a line, and you shall die in an unclean land, and Israel shall be led away captive from its land.’” Since you see that this was done by him who willed that truth and correction be proclaimed to his people when they went astray, why do you call us insolent, why insulting, because we tell you, who are wandering, what is true, because we do not listen to your voice saying, “Do not believe as the patriarchs, prophets, apostles and martyrs believed, but believe as Arius taught”? In what respect are we found proud in your eyes? Only in this: that we curse your sacrileges and shun your commands as we would swords and poisons. We are not the first to have done this; all those who have already pleased God by holding the faith we preach have done the same. None of his servants feared to suffer death for God; none of his household gave a thought to the kinds of torture inflicted by you tyrants, but kept his commandments before their eyes. So Tobit was found glorious and distinguished before the Lord, because he feared not the edict of that king, your fellow in damnation, but God almighty alone. That this is so, believe Tobit himself, who says: “When King Sennacherib came fleeing from Judea because of the judgment which the Lord had executed on him for the blasphemies he had uttered, he killed many of the children of Israel in his anger; but I wrapped their bodies and buried them. And it was reported to the king that I was burying them, and he sought to kill me. But I fled, and all my property was plundered, and nothing was left to me but my wife Anna and my son Tobias. And it came to pass forty-five days later that his sons killed that king, and Esarhaddon his son reigned there in his place. And when I had come to my house and my wife Anna and my son Tobias had been restored to me, at Pentecost, our feast, which is the holy feast of weeks, a good dinner was prepared for me, and I reclined to dine, and the table was set before me, and I saw a great many dishes, and I said to my son Tobias: ‘Go and bring any poor man you find among our brethren who are captives in Nineveh, but one who keeps God in mind with all his heart; bring him, and let him eat this dinner together with me. See, I am waiting for you, my son, until you come.’ And Tobias went out to look for some poor captive among our brethren, and he came back and said to me: ‘Father.’ And I said: ‘What is it, my son?’ And he said to me: ‘Look, one of our nation has been killed, strangled with a noose, and thrown out.’ And I went out, leaving my dinner before I had tasted anything of it, and I took him up from the street into a room near me, so that I could bury him after the sun had set. And I returned and washed and ate my dinner in mourning, and I remembered the word of the prophet Amos which he spoke at Bethel, saying: ‘Your feast days shall be turned into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation’; and I wept. And after the sun had set, I went and dug a grave and buried him. And all my neighbors mocked me, saying: ‘How is it that this man is not afraid? He has already been hunted down to be killed for this very thing, and he fled, and once again he has begun burying the dead.’”

So when you see that the servants of God have never feared the cruelty of you tyrants and cannot fear it now, but have always kept the Lord's commands in mind and keep them still, how can you see fit to judge us insolent? Plainly it is because, by God's doing, we trample your power like mud. Our own strength does not do this. It is the gift of the mercy of the one whom you see fit to curse in us. God says to the prophet Ezekiel: "Son of man, I am sending you to the house of Israel, because they have embittered me, they and their fathers, to this very day. And you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord — whether they hear or tremble, for it is an embittering house — and they will know that you are a prophet among them. And you, son of man, do not fear them or tremble before their faces, for they will rage and run together against you on every side, and you dwell in the midst of scorpions. Do not fear their words and do not tremble before their faces, for it is an embittering house. And you shall speak my words to them, in case they hear or are afraid, for it is an embittering house." We seem obstinate to you, just as this prophet, devoted to God alone, seemed to those whose darkness you follow. That is exactly why the prophet Ezekiel seemed obstinate to the Jews, your fellow apostates, and arrogant to the kings of Israel: because he carried out the Lord's commands and told them what God had commanded him to say. You are right to call us arrogant, we through whom God willed [?] all his commands to be brought to the knowledge of the believing peoples. You are right, I say, to brand us, the bishops of God, as insolent, if we tell you what God has willed to be said to you. You hate those who love you and persecute those who wish you well, but we cannot fear the gnashing teeth of your butchery. For you hear the Lord say: "And you, son of man, do not fear them or tremble before their faces, for they will rage and run together against you on every side, and you dwell in the midst of scorpions. Do not fear their words, do not tremble before their faces, for it is an embittering house." I say that we cannot fear the threats of your imperial power, because your scorpion's strength has no force against us. You can see that we are shielded by the power of God, and you can see that God is our defender and protector. So we will not stop pressing the Lord's commands on you, and we keep our fear for him alone, who says: "Son of man, go in to the house of Israel and speak my words to them. For you are not sent to Israel as to a people of deep speech, nor to many peoples of another voice or another tongue, nor to those heavy of tongue, whose speech you will not understand. If I had sent you to such as these, they might perhaps have listened to your words. But the house of Israel will not be willing to listen to you, because they are not willing to listen to me, for the whole house of Israel is contentious and hard of heart. And behold, I have made your face strong against their faces, and I will strengthen your constancy against their contentiousness, and you will always be firmer than rock. Do not be afraid of them or dismayed before their faces, for it is an embittering house." Which of us could fear you? You can see that God's power has made us solid and firm to beat back your defiance, and that we stand unmoved with our feet planted against your rage, as rocks of massive bulk stand against the swelling sea. That is why you judge us your enemies: because we press you to turn from a scorpion into a servant of God. For you cannot now doubt that you are one of the scorpions, one of those of whom you have heard the Lord say to the prophet: "And you, son of man, do not fear or tremble before their faces, for they will rage and run together against you on every side, and you dwell in the midst of scorpions." That is why we seem to wrong you: because you see that we call you a scorpion. If God had not said that you are a scorpion, you would be right to call me insulting. But as it is, your own deeds show that you are a scorpion, and you cry out in vain that you suffer insult from us. God says that you are a scorpion, and are you angry with me for calling you by that name? What insult is it if you are told: "Unless you turn to God, you will always be what you are now, one of the scorpions, one of the most monstrous enemies of God"?

Read through the rest of the prophet Ezekiel, and then dare to call me insolent, arrogant, insulting and obstinate: "And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, behold, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel, and you will hear a word from my mouth and warn them from me. When I say to the wicked man, 'You shall surely die,' and you have not warned him or spoken to warn the wicked man to turn from his ways so that he may live, that wicked man shall die in his iniquity, and I will require his blood at your hand. But if you warn the wicked man and he does not turn from his wickedness and his way, that wicked man shall die in his iniquity, and you will have delivered your soul. And when a righteous man turns away from his righteous deeds and commits sin, and I set a torment before his face, he shall die, because you did not warn him. He shall die in his sins, because his righteous deeds will not be remembered, and I will require his blood at your hand. But if you warn the righteous man not to forsake the right, and he does not forsake it, that righteous man shall surely live, because you warned him, and you will have saved your soul." What do you say to this, Constantius? Must the priests of God keep silent and hide his divine commands, or is it right to lay open to you all the Lord's precepts? Shall we convey the whole will of God to those entrusted to us, or shall we cheat ourselves of it and so cut our own throats? For the Lord says that he will require your blood from me. But if you do not obey God, whose divine warnings we press on you, you will die a wicked man in your own wickedness, and the salvation of your soul will no longer be required of us. For we were not terrified by your threats. We feared only him who commanded that no one but himself is to be feared, and we confronted you in the name of the Lord God so that you might rescue yourself from your abominable paths. What ought I to have done so as not to seem to insult you, the emperor, at a time when, I declare, you were born to turn us, the servants of God, away from the way of truth? When Nebuchadnezzar had sent Holofernes, the commander of his army, and he was besieging Jerusalem, what did Judith pray to God for? Surely that he would destroy the enemies of Israel. Did she not say: "Watch over those who rise up against your house"? "O Lord God of my father Simeon, you gave him a sword to take vengeance on the foreigners who violated a virgin's womb to defile her, bared her thigh to her ruin and defiled her womb to her disgrace. For you said, 'It shall not be so,' and you acted. Therefore you gave their rulers to slaughter, and their bed, which had received the beloved, to blood. You struck down slaves along with the mighty, the mighty on their thrones. You gave their wives as plunder and their daughters into captivity, and all their spoil to be divided among your beloved sons, who were zealous with your zeal, abhorred the defilement of their race and called on you for help. My God, hear me, a widow. For you made what came before those things, and those things, and what followed after, and what is now, and what is still to come. All your ways are prepared, and your creation lies in your foresight. For behold, the Assyrians are swollen with their strength. They are exalted in horse and rider, they glory in the arm of their foot soldiers, they put their hope in shields and the drawn bow and slings, and they do not know that you are the Lord who crushes wars. The Lord is your name. Cast down their strength, O Eternal One; crush their host by your power, and bring down their stubbornness in your wrath. For they have planned to bring your holy things to nothing, to defile the tabernacle where your glorious name rests, and to seize the horn of your altar with iron. Look upon their pride. Give into my hand, a widow's hand, the strength I have planned, and by my persuasive lips strike their mouth, the servant with the ruler and the ruler upon his servant. Shatter his might by the hand of a widow. For your power does not lie in numbers, nor your might and your gift in the strong. You are the God of the lowly, the help of the weak, the support of the feeble, the savior of those in despair. Yes, God of my father and God of Israel's inheritance, Lord, ruler of heaven and earth, creator of the waters, king of all creation, hear my prayer. Give me cunning and persuasion to wound and bruise those who have plotted harsh things against your covenant, your holy house, the heights of Zion and the house your sons possess. Make every nation and every tribe know that you are the God of all power and might, and that there is no other protector of the race of Israel but you."

What will your wise mind see fit to make of this? After this prayer poured out to God against the enemies of religion, can you possibly say that we do wrong in striving against you? Is it wrong for us to tell you: "Either correct your crooked ways and stop delighting in the power of your empire, or know that you will come to nothing"? What else are we, the servants of God and priests of his divine majesty, doing today but what those men did whose imitators we long to be found? For I think it right not to abandon the peoples entrusted to us in this great persecution you have brought on them, but to encourage them. They should know that he whose servants we are is able to snatch us from the hands of his enemies, and that you, the enemy of God's house, are not to be feared. They should see that you are nothing, since our almighty God and Lord will bring to nothing all the impious undertakings you have set up against his house. What wrong are we doing you here? What insult do the bishops of the living God offer the Roman emperor if you are urged to gain eternal life, or are told that because you have taken up arms against the house of God, you will perish in great ruin unless you correct yourself? Why do we hold up before you the destruction of all the enemies of God's house? Only so that either fear of God may terrify you into changing, or, if you bring eternal punishment on yourself, we may triumph in safety on every side. Your blood cannot then be required of us by God, and we shall have seen the destruction of his church's adversaries. Persist, then, in this injustice of yours, and you will find what such deserts bring you. "Lucifer is puffed up with pride," you say — because he tells you the truth. What did you want me to do at this time, when you, the forerunner of Antichrist, took up arms against the house of God to kill us? At this time, when you have come forward as a denier of the only Son of God? Should I have kept silent and let you, the wolf, come to ravage God's flock? Or do you think it would have been right for us shepherds to go out to meet you while you stood ready, with parched throat, to devour us and those entrusted to us? Was it a great enough deed that this woman Judith, longing to please God, killed the enemy with her own hand, while we, appointed shepherds by the Lord, should not resist you even with a word? The Lord says in the Gospel: "The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep. The hireling, who is not the shepherd and does not own the sheep, sees the wolf coming and leaves the sheep and flees; and the wolf seizes them and scatters them, because he is a hireling and does not care about the sheep." So what were we to do so as not to seem to have insulted you? We recognized you as a wolf. We saw you stretch out your hands against the Lord's sheep. We watched you try to tear apart, all at once, everyone who calls on the Lord's name. Would it have been right for us to show ourselves hirelings instead of shepherds? He says to blessed Peter, "Feed my lambs," and again, "Feed my sheep." And do you want those who are found to be the successors of blessed Peter to play the part of hirelings when the wolf comes? These are the shepherds he long ago promised his people through Jeremiah, saying: "And I will give you shepherds after my own heart, and they will feed you, feeding you with discipline." He did not say: "I will give you the emperor Constantius, who can turn you into the devil's prey." You may say that we do wrong because we resist your sacrilege, shielded by the power of God.

Let us also see what was done, at the time when your fellow tyrant Antiochus arose as persecutor of our religion, by those who remembered that no one but God is to be feared. But first you should learn what he, whom you resemble, wrote. Then you will be able to see that those servants of God, whose companions we long to be found, resisted the sacrilege of Antiochus just as we, by God's favor, resist you. Holy Scripture speaks thus in the first book of Maccabees: "And the king wrote to his whole kingdom that all should be one people and that each should abandon his own laws. All the nations accepted the king's word, and many from Israel consented along with them and profaned the sabbath. The king sent books by the hand of messengers to Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, ordering them to follow the laws of a foreign land: to forbid burnt offerings, sacrifice and libation in the sanctuary, to defile the sabbaths and feast days, to pollute the sanctuary, to set up shrines and idols, to sacrifice swine and common animals, to leave their sons uncircumcised and to defile their souls with every uncleanness and abomination, so that they would forget the law and change the ordinances. And whoever did not act according to the king's word was to die. In accordance with all these words he sent written orders to his whole kingdom and appointed overseers over the people. And he ordered the cities of Judah to offer sacrifice, city by city. Many of the people gathered to them, everyone who forsook the law, and they did evil in the land." And further on: "They built the abomination of desolation upon the altar, and in the cities of Judah round about they built altars and burned incense at the doors of houses and in the streets. Any books of the law that they found they tore up and burned with fire. If a book of the covenant was found with anyone, or if anyone consented to the law, the king's decree put him to death. In their strength they did this to Israel, to those who were found in the cities month after month. And on the twenty-fourth of the month they offered sacrifice on the altar that stood upon the altar. The women who had circumcised their children they put to death according to the command. They hung the infants from their mothers' necks, and through their houses [?], and those who had circumcised them. But many in Israel held firm and were strengthened in themselves not to eat what was common, and they chose to die rather than be defiled by food and profane the holy covenant. And very great wrath came upon Israel in those days. Then Mattathias son of John, son of Simeon, a priest of the sons of Joarib, arose from Jerusalem. He had five sons." And further on: "And he saw the blasphemies that were being committed in Judah and in Israel, and said: Woe is me! Why was I born to see the ruin of the holy city? And they sat there while the sanctuary was given into the hand of enemies, into the hand of foreigners." And further on: "All her adornment has been taken away; from a free woman she has become a slave. Behold, our sanctuary and our beauty and our glory have been laid waste, and the nations have defiled them. Why should we live any longer? And Mattathias and his sons tore their garments, covered themselves with sackcloth and mourned greatly. Then the king's officers who were enforcing the apostasy came to the city of Modein to make them offer sacrifice. Many of Israel went over to them, and Mattathias and his sons gathered together. Those sent by the king answered and said to Mattathias: You are a leader, honored and great in this city, and supported by sons and brothers. Now come forward first and carry out the king's command, as all the nations have done, and the men of Judah, and those left in Israel. Then you and your sons will be friends of the king, and you and your sons will be honored with silver and gold and many gifts. Mattathias answered and said in a loud voice: Even if all the nations in the king's dominion obey him, each departing from the worship of his fathers, and have chosen to follow his commands, I and my sons will walk in the covenant of our fathers. May the Lord be gracious to us; we will not forsake the law and the ordinances. We will not listen to the king's word, and we will not turn aside from the service of our worship to the right or to the left. When he had finished speaking these words, a Jew came forward in the sight of all to offer sacrifice in Modein according to the king's command. Mattathias saw it and was filled with zeal. His loins trembled, and he gave vent to his anger according to judgment, and he ran to the altar and killed him. At the same time he killed the king's man who was compelling them to sacrifice, and he tore down the altar. Thus he showed zeal for the law, as Phinehas did to Zimri son of Salu. And Mattathias cried out in the city with a loud voice, saying: Let everyone who is zealous for the law and upholds the covenant come out after me. And he and his sons fled to the mountains and left behind everything they had in the city."

What have you seen us do that compares with this, that you should see fit to say, "Lucifer has insulted me"? Mattathias killed the king's officer with the sword, and also the man of his own people whom he had seen [?] the king's edict above God's. But I resist you and your people only with words and say: "I do not abandon the apostolic and evangelical faith; I believe as our fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob believed." And for this you accuse me of insults. If you had fallen into the hands of this Mattathias, zealous for God, or into the hand of Phinehas, to whom God bears witness through Moses in Numbers, and had tried to live in the manner of foreigners, they would without doubt have killed you with the sword, those who were slayers with the sword [?]. But I, because I wound with words that mind of yours soaked in the blood of Christians, am judged by you guilty of insults. Why, emperor, do you not avenge yourself on me? Why do you not deign to defend yourself against these insults and take vengeance on a beggar? Why do you not see to it? Not because you are unwilling, but because power has not yet been given you by the one to whom I trust I belong. Trusting in him, I speak freely to you about the things that seem wicked to me in your abominable deeds. You have seen that we have renounced you and all the riches of your kingdom, and your father too, and you have observed closely that we have promised never in any way to depart from the faith. So know that we are greatly amazed that you spare us, when you are in the habit of devouring with the edge of the sword those who displease you. I suppose it is out of piety, and we can well believe this of your gentleness. For I have been able to gather that, out of your excessive kindness, you have never killed anyone. You say: "He is proud." Why do I seem proud to you? Surely because you hear from me that you are doing what the enemies of God's religion have always done. It is my duty to press these things on you, since you are a heretic. Or are you not a heretic? But if you are a heretic, why do you accuse me of wronging you, when I do against you what God willed [?] me to do? The most holy prophet Jeremiah says that God said to him: "And you, gird up your loins, arise and speak all that I have commanded you. Do not fear before their faces or be afraid in their sight." Since this is so, and the necessity of the office God has laid on us compels us to tell you, as you go on acting this way, whatever God has commanded to be said to you, only two courses remain. Either you obey God's commands when I confront you, I who am a servant and priest of his clemency, or you prove from the sacred Scriptures, perhaps on the ground that you are king, that I am not permitted to confront you in the name of the Lord so that you may correct yourself. If you cannot prove that this is forbidden me, and instead begin to find that I am commanded to reprove you, rebuke you, exhort you, entreat you, admonish you and urge you to please God, why do you say that I am insulting you? For he gave us, his bishops, such power to rebuke and teach you who are entrusted to us that he said: "Do not fear before their faces, do not be afraid in their sight. Behold, I have set you this day as a fortified city and as a strong bronze wall against all the kings of Judah and its princes and the people of the land. They will fight against you, but they will not prevail against you, for I am with you to deliver you, says the Lord." What were the things Jeremiah said to the kings of Judah, its princes and the peoples of the land? Surely these: that they had forsaken the Lord and sacrificed to foreign gods. You too have done this and are doing it still. You have forsaken the apostolic and evangelical faith, you have taken up the Arian heresy, and you are forcing all the servants of God to become idolaters. Because you dare to do these things, you call those who want to secure your salvation proud. God says to Jeremiah: "And you, gird up your loins and arise, and speak all that I tell you. Do not fear before their faces or be afraid in their sight." And you, Emperor Constantius, are indignant that we say to you in your error: "Return to the way of salvation; abandon the error that Arius devised at the devil's prompting."

God commands that he alone be feared; he has laid down that no one besides him is to be dreaded. And have you decreed that things be carried out which would take away the fear of the Lord and make you the one to be dreaded? God says to Jeremiah: “Behold, I have made you this day like a fortified city and like a strong wall of bronze against all the kings of Judah and its princes and the people of the land. And they will fight against you, but they will not prevail against you, for I am with you to deliver you, says the Lord.” And do you suppose that you can be feared by any of the servants of God? Why do you call me arrogant and proud? Why do you call me insulting? Surely because I have found you, by your works, to be one of those of whom blessed John says: “You have heard that antichrist is coming; but now there are many antichrists.” So you brand us guilty of wrongdoing, as though we were the first to resist you, to keep you from bringing your idolatry into the church of God. You have read in the first book of Maccabees: “And each man said to his neighbour: If we all do as our brothers have done, and do not fight against the gentiles for our lives and our ordinances, they will soon destroy us from the earth. And they took counsel on that day, saying: Whoever comes against us in battle on the sabbath day, let us fight against him, and we shall not all die, as our brothers died in their hiding places. Then there gathered to them an assembly strong in might from Israel, everyone who was devoted to the law; and all who were fleeing from the evils joined them and became a support to them. And they struck down a force, and struck the sinners in their wrath and wicked men in their indignation; and the rest fled to the gentiles to save themselves. And Mattathias and his friends went about and destroyed the altars, and they forcibly circumcised all the uncircumcised boys they found within the borders of Israel; and they pursued the sons of pride, and the work prospered in their hands; and they rescued the law from the hands of the gentiles and of kings, and they did not yield the horn to the sinner.” What does your mind, wounded by the poisons of Arius, deign to think of this? What can your heart, torn by the serpent’s bites, devise against this defence of ours? When you observe that those men did these things, ought we to have kept silent while blasphemies uttered by your mouth wounded the people divinely entrusted to us? “And Mattathias,” it says, “and his friends went about and destroyed the altars, and they forcibly circumcised all the uncircumcised boys they found within the borders of Israel; and they pursued the sons of pride, and the work prospered in their hands; and they rescued the law from the hands of the gentiles and of kings, and they did not yield the horn to the sinner.” Since those who acted in this way became most dear to God, was it fitting that we, by flattering you and running along with you in your crime, should become, as you are, God’s bitterest enemies? If we seem to you to wrong you on this account, because we could not accept your idolatry, produce for me, I beg you, a single one of the worshippers of God who spared the adversaries of his religion. In the second book of Ezra, to those who opposed their rebuilding the house and the temple and the city in Jerusalem for the Lord, he says: “The God of heaven himself will prosper us, and we his servants will rise up and build; but you have no portion and no remembrance in Jerusalem.” And further on, when the adversaries said: “Will they sacrifice, or eat in their place? Will not a fox go up and break down their stone walls?”, Ezra his servant says this to God: “Hear, O our God, for we have become despised; turn their taunts back upon their own heads, and give them up to be a derision in a land of captivity; and do not cover their iniquity, and let their sins not be blotted out from before your face.”

What have we said about you that is anything like this? He to whom Ezra prayed is my witness—he to whom I too pray, and to whom his blessed church, my church, established throughout the whole world, prays—that our prayers for you are these: that you correct your errors and become one of us. Observe, meanwhile, how the men of God neither feared their adversaries nor ceased pouring out prayer against the enemies of God’s house, so that the forces of the adversaries of God’s religion might be brought to nothing. For so too the most holy Moses says to God in the song of Exodus: “Let fear and trembling at the greatness of your arm fall upon them; let them become like stones until your people pass over, until your people pass over, O Lord, this people whom you have acquired.” Those men spoke such words to God against those delivered up to them; yet because we say to you, “Either turn to God, or else be certain that God will bring all your empty pride to nothing,” we seem to you impudent. Consider further what Mattathias did, that most holy man devoted to God, after the illustrious deeds he had performed, and what he said to his sons at the end of his life, and see whether we, the priests of God, are not acting against you in the right way. Holy scripture speaks, saying: “The days drew near for Mattathias to die, and he said to his sons: Now pride and chastisement have grown strong, and it is a time of overthrow and of wrathful indignation. Now, my sons, be zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of our fathers. Remember the works of the fathers which they did in their generations, and you will receive great glory and an everlasting name. Was not Abraham found faithful in temptation, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness? Joseph in the time of his distress kept the commandment, and became lord of Egypt. Phinehas our father, being zealous with zeal, received the covenant of an everlasting priesthood. Joshua, in fulfilling the word, became leader in Israel. Caleb, in bearing witness in the assembly, received an inheritance. David by his mercy obtained the throne of the kingdom for ever. Elijah, being zealous with zeal for the law, was taken up into heaven. Hananiah, Azariah and Mishael, believing, were delivered from the flame. Daniel in his innocence was delivered from the mouth of the lions. And so consider, from generation to generation, that none who hope in him will be weakened. Do not fear the words of a sinful man, for his glory is dung and worms. Today he is exalted, and tomorrow he will not be found, because he has returned to his earth and his scheming will perish. My sons, take courage and be strong in the law, for by it you will be glorious. And here is Simeon your brother; I know that he is a man of counsel; listen to him, and he will be a father to you. And let Judas Maccabeus, mighty in strength from his youth, be the commander of your army, and he will fight the battle. Gather to yourselves all who keep the law, and avenge the wrong done to your people; pay back the gentiles what they deserve, and give heed to the commandment of the law.” When, then, you see that he gave such commands to his sons and ordered them to do what he himself had also done, since he teaches that this is how the patriarchs, the prophets and all the righteous pleased God, what did you want us to do, you man of darkness, so as not to seem defiant to you? Should we, the living, have yielded to you, the dead—servants of God to a henchman of the devil—when you see this Mattathias saying to his sons: “And so consider, from generation to generation, that none who hope in him will be weakened. Do not fear the words of a sinful man, for his glory is dung and worms. Today he is exalted, and tomorrow he will not be found, because he has returned to his earth and his scheming will perish”? So as not to seem to wrong you, are we to spare you while you destroy the house of God—you who are here today and tomorrow will be worms and dung—and so bring upon ourselves God’s displeasure, and deserve to be brought to nothing along with you?

Learn next what the sons of this most devout Mattathias also did: whether they feared the hand of your fellow butcher, whether they kept his army before their eyes rather than our Lord, in whom they believed as almighty, as we believe, and so rose up against the enemy with all their strength. “And Judas, called Maccabeus, his son, rose up in his place. All his brothers helped him, and all who had joined his father; and they fought the battle of Israel with gladness. He spread the glory of his people, and put on a breastplate like a giant, and girded on his weapons of war, and set battles in array, protecting the camp with the sword. In his deeds he became like a lion, like a lion’s whelp roaring for prey. He pursued the wicked, searching them out, and those who troubled his people he burned. The wicked shrank back for fear of him, and all the workers of iniquity were thrown into confusion, and deliverance prospered in his hand. He embittered many kings and gladdened Jacob by his deeds, and his memory is blessed for ever. He went through the cities of Judah and destroyed all the ungodly out of it, and turned away wrath from Israel. He was renowned to the ends of the earth, and he gathered together those who were perishing.” Those men, fired with such zeal, acted against the enemies of God’s house; and were we not to rise up against you, for fear of being called impudent? Rather, you would rightly call me impudent if we had not rightly scorned your sacrilegious edict. For look at what the leaders of the Jews, your fellow reprobates, commanded the apostles, and what, on the other hand, the company of the blessed apostles did, and you will find that we are not impudent, but desire the good of both you and ourselves. “Now Peter and John were going up into the temple at the ninth hour, the hour of prayer. And a certain man, lame from his mother’s womb, was being carried there, whom they laid every day at the gate of the temple called Beautiful, so that he might ask alms of those going into the temple. When he saw Peter and John about to enter the temple, he asked for alms. Peter, with John, looked intently at him and said: Look at us. And he looked at them, hoping to receive something from them. But Peter said to him: Silver and gold I do not have, but what I have I give you: in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, rise and walk. And taking him by the right hand he raised him up, and at once his feet and ankles were made strong; and leaping up he stood and walked, and went into the temple with them, walking and leaping and praising God. And all the people saw him walking and praising God, and they recognized that he was the one who used to sit for alms at the Beautiful Gate of the temple, and they were filled with awe and amazement at what had happened to him.” And further on: “As they were speaking these words to the people, the priests and the captain of the temple and the Sadducees came upon them, annoyed that they were teaching the people and proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection of the dead; and they laid hands on them and put them in custody.” And further on: “Seeing the boldness of Peter and John, and finding that they were unlearned and illiterate men, they marvelled; and they recognized them as men who had been with Jesus. And seeing the man who had been healed standing with them, they had nothing to say in reply. But when they had ordered them to go outside the council, they conferred with one another, saying: What shall we do with these men? For it is plain to all who live in Jerusalem that a notable sign has been done through them, and we cannot deny it. But so that these words may spread no further among the people, let us threaten them not to speak any more in this name to anyone. And when all agreed, they called them in and charged them not to speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus. But Peter and John answered and said: Whether it is right in the sight of God to listen to you rather than to God, you must judge; for we cannot help speaking of what we have seen and heard. And after threatening them they let them go, finding no way to punish them because of the people; for all were glorifying God for what had happened. For the man on whom this sign of healing had been performed was more than forty years old. When they were released, they went to their own people and reported all that the chief priests and the elders had said to them. And when they heard it, they lifted their voices to the Lord with one mind and said: Lord, you are the God who made heaven and earth and the sea and all that is in them, who by the Holy Spirit, through the mouth of our father David your servant, said: Why did the nations rage, and the peoples plot in vain? The kings of the earth took their stand, and the rulers gathered together against the Lord and against his Christ. For truly in this city there gathered together against your holy Son Jesus, whom you anointed, Herod and Pontius Pilate with the gentiles and the peoples of Israel, to do whatever your hand and your counsel had predestined. And now, Lord, look upon their threats, and grant to your servants to speak your word with all boldness, while you stretch out your hand to heal and to perform signs and wonders through the name of your holy Son Jesus. And when they had prayed, the place where they were gathered was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke the word of God with all boldness.”

If you have now grasped why we have brought all this forward, if you have thoroughly absorbed the whole purpose of our argument, will you dare to say any longer that we are impudent? For you see that the blessed apostles neither gave way to the leaders of the Jews nor yielded to their threats, but always fearlessly carried through what had been entrusted to them; and that likewise the people of God not only were not terrified by the threats of the unbelievers, but even prayed that God would deign to grant his apostles boldness in speaking and steadfastness in defending the truth. If, then, this was done both by the blessed apostles and by the peoples dedicated to God, and they were not called defiant or impudent by God for resisting his enemies, how is it that we are called proud, impudent and insulting by you—we who, sinners though we are, still hold the holy faith of the apostles and of those peoples who believed in the only Son of God? We are proud along with the apostles, then, because we, soldiers of Christ, count as nothing your voice, apostate, and your terrors, sacrilegious man; because we preach the Son of God as the true Son of God, just as the most blessed apostles preached him. So we seem to you shameless, impudent and proud, just as the most holy apostles seemed to the Jews; and if the apostles were in the body today, you could have said to them the very things you deign to say to us. For we find that it was constantly commanded them, by the mouth of your fellow blasphemers—the scribes, the Pharisees, the rulers and the high priest of the Jews—that they should not teach or preach the only Son of God. Yet hear further what is written of what they did, in case your heart, fattened on darkness, may at some point be brought to see the truth: “By the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders were done among the people. And they were all together with one mind in Solomon’s Portico; none of the rest dared to join them, but the people held them in high esteem. And more and more believers were added to the Lord, multitudes of men and women, so that they even carried the sick out into the streets and laid them on beds and pallets, so that when Peter came by at least his shadow might fall on some of them; and they were freed from their infirmities. A multitude also gathered from the towns around Jerusalem, bringing the sick and those tormented by unclean spirits, and they were all healed. But the high priest rose up, and all who were with him, the sect of the Sadducees, and filled with jealousy they laid hands on the apostles and put them in custody. But an angel of the Lord opened the prison doors and brought them out, saying: Go, stand in the temple, and speak to the people all the words of this life. When they heard this, they entered the temple at daybreak and taught. Then the high priest came, and those who were with him, and they called together the council and the whole assembly of the sons of Israel, and sent to the prison to have them brought. But the officers came and did not find them in the prison, and they returned and reported, saying: We found the prison securely locked and the guards standing at the door, but when we opened it we found no one inside. When the chief priests and the high priest heard these words, they were at a loss about them, wondering what this could mean. Then someone came and reported to them, saying: Look, the men whom you put in custody are standing in the temple and teaching the people. Then the captain went with the officers and brought them, but not by force, for they were afraid of the people, that they might be stoned. When they had brought them, they set them before the council. And the priest questioned them, saying: We strictly charged you not to teach in this name, and look, you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching, and you mean to bring that man’s blood upon us. But Peter and the apostles answered, saying: Must one obey God or men?” If, then, God must be obeyed and not men, why do you call us defiant, why do you call us insulting, when you see that we obey the commands of God? “When they heard this they were enraged,” says scripture, “and planned to kill them.” So you too hold us in custody and threaten to kill us, because you are possessed by the same spirit that held the Jews captive and holds them still. If you are not held captive by that unclean spirit, why do you forbid us to confess and preach the only Son of God? The angel of God, bringing the apostles out of the prison of the Jews, your fellow desperadoes, said: “Go, teach in the temple the words of this life”; and you, removing priests from the church of God, thought they should be thrown into prison, so that we might not preach the word of life.

Meanwhile, I beg you to answer: what is the difference between you and your fellow Scotinus, whom the people of Sirmium, turning the name the other way round, call Photinus? You are asked to set out what separates you and how you differ. See: if in those days the rulers, the high priest and the whole council of the Jews said to the apostles, “You mean to bring this man's blood upon us,” Photinus too professes that the Son of God is a mere man, and says that he did not exist before blessed Mary. Your profession is this: that the Son of God does indeed exist before all things, that is, before the heavens, the earth, the sea and everything in them, but that he came to be out of nothing, that he is a creature. What difference do you suppose there is between you and Paul of Samosata, or this disciple of his, your fellow Scotinus, except that you say “before all things” and he says “after all things”? For the rest, you share one cruel and unbelieving mind: you both say that God has no true Son. Look, by contrast, at how the holy church believes: We believe in one God, the Father almighty, maker of things visible and invisible; and in one Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God, begotten of the Father, that is, of the substance of the Father, God from God, Light from Light, true God from true God, begotten not made, of one substance with the Father, which the Greeks call homoousion, through whom all things were made, both those in heaven and those on earth; who for us men and for our salvation came down, was made flesh, became man, suffered, rose again on the third day, ascended into heaven, and will come to judge the living and the dead; and we believe in the Holy Spirit. You see that this is the apostolic and evangelical faith, which maintains that the Son has always reigned and reigns with the Father, and which confesses that the divine Trinity is perfect and has one substance. Otherwise, what difference would there be between the church and you heretics or the Jews, if the blessed church did not believe thus? What holy faith would there be?
