So that you may know what the Lord's church condemns in you, it has said and still says of you: “But those who say, ‘There was a time when he was not,’ and ‘Before he was begotten he was not,’ and that he was made out of things that did not exist, or from another substance, saying that the Son of God is mutable and changeable, these the catholic and apostolic church anathematizes.” For this holy faith the apostles were shut up in prison, received chains, and were tormented with beatings hour after hour, to keep them from revealing the truth to the world; and yet they would not stop [?] preaching, even until they were slain. And you say that we are men of the greatest insolence, because, of course, we keep to the way of the apostles, because we tell you that you have gone astray, as blessed John the Baptist did to Herod. “But Herod the tetrarch, when he was rebuked by him because of Herodias, his brother's wife, and for all the evils that Herod had done, added this to them all: he shut John up in prison.” Why did Herod shut John up? Surely because his deeds were being exposed. That is how you too deal with God's servants, because we say to you: Do not do what you are doing; do not be a murderer; do not persecute the Lord's church; do not reject the apostolic faith and approve the heretical one; do not bring idolatry into the church. We consider that we say these things above all for your salvation; and if you refuse to restrain yourself, you will without doubt be seeking eternal death for yourself, just as Herod sought it. For he could not harm John, whether by throwing him into prison or by killing him, since you see that John is the friend of God, while Herod is the enemy of God. Seeking to harm us, who long for eternal safety to be granted to you, you persecute us in every way; but the powers of your authority will not be able to harm the servants of God's only Son, because you are found to be one of those whom he made subject to us believers, saying: “Behold, I have given you power to tread on serpents and scorpions and over all the might of the enemy; and nothing shall harm you.” You who call me proud because I tell you the truth: what kind of man do you want me to be found to be? That servant who received one talent, hid it, and handed back to his master only that one talent, and who, because he did not hand it back multiplied by interest as his fellow servants did, deserved to lose even that talent and to hear, “You wicked and lazy servant”? Or the one who handed back the sum he had received multiplied tenfold, and to whom it was said, “Well done, good and faithful servant; because you were faithful in a little, I will set you over much; enter into the joy of your master”? But how could I hear that if, fearing you, I did what pleases you? Look in the Gospel at what the Lord wanted us to do, and stop calling us arrogant: “A certain rich man went into a far country to receive a kingdom and to return. And he called ten servants and gave them ten talents and said to them, ‘Trade with this until I come.’ But his citizens hated him and sent an embassy after him, saying, ‘We do not want this man to reign over us.’ And it came to pass that when he returned, having received the kingdom, he ordered the servants to whom he had given the money to be called, so that he might know how much each had gained by trading. The first came, saying, ‘Lord, your talent has gained ten talents.’ And he said to him, ‘Well done, good servant; because you were faithful in a little, you shall have authority over ten cities.’ And another came, saying, ‘Lord, your mina has made five talents.’ And he said to this one too, ‘You, be over five cities.’ And another came, saying, ‘Here is your talent, which I kept laid away in a napkin; for I was afraid of you, because you are a hard man: you take up what you did not lay down and reap what you did not sow.’ And the master said to him, ‘Out of your own mouth I judge you, faithless servant. You knew that I am a hard man, taking up what I did not lay down and reaping what I did not sow; why then did you not put my money in the bank, so that when I came I could have collected it with interest?’ And to those standing by he said [?], ‘Take the talent from him and give it to the one who has ten talents. For I tell you, to everyone who has, more will be given; but from the one who has not, even what he has will be taken away. But as for those enemies of mine who did not want me to reign over them, bring them here and kill them before me.’”

Clearly, if you do not change, you will be one of those who were ordered to be killed. This is why I seem proud to you: because I want you not to be killed, because I long for you, too, to be found in that sum entrusted to me, which I desire to see multiplied. Because we wrestle with you in this way, we seem to you to be enemies, we who, keeping the precept of the blessed apostle, pour out prayer unceasingly for your welfare: “I urge, then, first of all, that supplications, prayers, petitions and thanksgivings be made for all men, for kings and for all who are in high positions, that we may lead a tranquil and quiet life in godliness and dignity. For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Savior, who wills all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.” We seem to you to be enemies, we who desire you to attain the knowledge of the truth; you call me insulting because I say what serves both your salvation and mine. But this very assertion of yours, which claims that I am doing you an injury, shows you to be unwise. For if only you had been wise! First, you would never have been found sacrilegious; and then, once rebuked by the authority of the sacred writings, you would by now have shown yourself a man of restraint. But as it is, because you are unwise, when a bishop says to you, “Emperor, look to your salvation, for you are weighed down by the enormous burdens of your crimes,” you say, “You are insulting me.” “I charge you before God,” says the apostle to Timothy, “and Christ Jesus and the elect angels, to keep these things without discrimination, doing nothing out of partiality,” but to keep to fairness. And you call him insulting who now rebukes you, caught in such great crimes, for having committed them, and who now pleads with you to rescue yourself from your evils while there is opportunity, and to be such a man as God will not punish among those whom he marks out as wicked and faithless, saying: “I have begotten sons and raised them up, but they have despised me.” This is why I seem proud to you: because I desire you to be found among those whom the only Son of God invites to his kingdom, saying: “Come, you blessed of my Father, receive the kingdom prepared for you from the beginning of the world.” You think that you suffer an insult because true things are said to you; the glorious apostle, on the contrary, commands: “Rebuke those who sin in the presence of all, so that the rest also may be afraid.” Whom ought I to heed? You, who say, “Let me destroy the religion of God, let me turn his servants over to the Antichrist, let me establish everyone in this sacrilege of mine”? Or the blessed apostle, who commands me to rebuke you, a sinner, in the presence of all? But if you think that I ought to have spared you because you are emperor, in this too you are found unwise. For you hear the apostle say, “Rebuke those who sin in the presence of all, so that the rest also may be afraid”; and you say, “You ought to have spared me especially, because I was king of the Roman empire.” And what then would I have done with this solemn charge: “I charge you before God and Christ Jesus and the elect angels, to keep these things without discrimination, doing nothing by leaning to one side”? This, surely, is why I seem to you to be insulting: because I have not set your commands above the commands of God. In the Acts of the Apostles I read that the blessed apostles were seized by those whose partner you are, not only in unbelief but also in cruelty, and that they were commanded not to teach in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. But let us look together at that very passage of sacred scripture, to see whether the apostles complied with the commands of the enemies of God's only Son, or whether they carried through most earnestly what they had undertaken to fulfil. “Calling in the apostles,” it says, “they beat them and released them, commanding them not to speak to anyone in the name of Jesus. So they went out from the presence of the council rejoicing that they had been counted worthy to suffer insult for the name. And every day, in the temple and at home, they did not cease teaching and proclaiming the good news of our Lord Jesus Christ.”

Since sacred scripture reports that the blessed apostles acted thus, are we, the appointed leaders of God's churches, to keep silent while you invite the hearts of all to deny the Son of God and busy yourself with strengthening your heresy, simply so that we may not be found to have been insulting to you, a blasphemer, a murderer, a destroyer of God's religion? Sacred scripture tells us that the apostles feared neither the beatings nor the threats of the sons of pestilence, but always went on teaching; were we, then, meant to be broken by the might of your perishable reign, so that you could carry out all your wicked designs? We are reckoned insolent by you because we tell you the truth. So too your fellow blasphemers judged the most blessed Stephen, because he said to them: “Stiff-necked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, you always resist the Holy Spirit; as your fathers did, so do you. Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute? They killed those who announced beforehand the coming of the Righteous One, whose betrayers and murderers you have now become, you who received the law as ordained by angels and did not keep it.” When the Jews heard this, were they rightly or wrongly roused against Stephen, the most holy martyr? If wrongly, then see that you too are wrongly roused against those who want you saved. Notice that you stand against God's church on the same side on which the Jews stood then and are standing now; that you are just as stiff-necked, just as uncircumcised in heart and ears. That is why, just as they could not bear to hear the truth but rushed to kill a worshiper of God, you too are rushing to kill us, who tell you what is sound and plain. “When they heard these things,” says divine scripture, “they were raging in their hearts and gnashing their teeth at him”; and further on: “But crying out with a loud voice, they stopped their ears and rushed at him with one mind, and having cast him out of the city they stoned him.” So you, raging in heart and gnashing your teeth, are against us for no other reason than that we call you a persecutor of God's house, a destroyer of God's religion, a shedder of the blood of Christ's servants; because we rightly call you sacrilegious, since you are a blasphemous heretic, since you make war on the apostolic and evangelical faith. We do nothing hateful to God if, dealing with you in this way in which we contend with you [?], we tell you what we understand you to be. For we find that the glorious men acted thus against such as you are. “While they were ministering to the Lord and fasting,” says scripture, “the Holy Spirit said: ‘Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.’ Then, after fasting and praying, they laid their hands on them and sent them off. So they, sent out by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia and from there sailed to Cyprus. And when they came to Salamis, they preached the word of the Lord in the synagogues of the Jews. They also had John as their assistant. And when they had gone through the whole island as far as Paphos, they found a certain man, a Jewish false prophet named Bar-Jesus, which means ‘Ready,’ who was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, a man of understanding. He summoned Barnabas and Saul and sought to hear the word of God. But Etoemus the magician (for so his name is said to be translated) opposed them, seeking to turn the proconsul away from the faith. But Saul, who is also Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, looked intently at him and said: ‘You who are full of all deceit and trickery, son of the devil, enemy of all righteousness, will you not stop perverting the straight ways of the Lord? And now, behold, the hand of the Lord is against you, and you will be blind, not seeing the sun for a time.’ And immediately mist and darkness fell upon him, and he went about seeking someone to lead him by the hand. Then the proconsul, seeing what had happened, believed, astonished with wonder at the teaching of the Lord.” We trust that, instructed by this testimony, you will not say: “Lucifer insults me, the emperor.”

What does it matter to me what you are, when I am saying the very things that the man who was recognized as a false prophet heard from the apostle? For I regard you, Emperor Constantius, just as the glorious Paul and Barnabas regarded Bar-Jesus the Jew. You are found to be opposed to the name of the Lord just as he was; you resist the truth just as he resisted it; you do not want men to believe in the only Son of God, but in yourself, as that Jewish false prophet did, for no other reason than that you are driven by a hostile spirit just as he was driven. For when you hear that the proconsul was a man of understanding who wished to be instructed by the blessed apostles so that he might grasp the way of truth, and that the man whom you imitate resisted the apostles to keep them from leading the proconsul to believe in the Son of God, it is plain that you are just such a man as that Jewish false prophet was. Again, since holy scripture says that Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, uttered that denunciation, you must understand that the Jewish false prophet was full of an unclean spirit. Just as he, driven by a hostile spirit, spoke in opposition, so, since you too are found resisting at the prompting of the adversary, you must judge yourself to be none other than Bar-Jesus, the Jewish false prophet. Therefore, since you understand that you are a second Bar-Jesus, a Jewish false prophet, as often as your sacrilegious mouth has said, “God has no true Son,” do not be offended if we say to you what the apostle said to your predecessor, the Jewish false prophet: you are full of all deceit and trickery, a son of the devil, an enemy of all righteousness, who will not stop perverting the straight ways of the Lord. If you are upset that the things said to him are said to you, whose road of death you are following, you will show yourself very foolish, wanting to be what that son, the Jewish false prophet, was, and yet not wanting to be called by the names by which he too was called. Again I urge and implore you, and also warn you, to be willing to look to your own good, so that eternal punishment may not take you. For if he deserved to be blinded because he tried to resist, consider what evils may be in store for you, a murderer, a sacrilegious man, a destroyer of God's religion, both in this life and for ever. Hear further what can teach you that we are not insulting, but truthful. Those seven most glorious brothers resisted Antiochus, just as we have now resisted you. You have read what the fourth answered your fellow pestilence, you who see fit to keep shouting that I am insulting because I tell you that unless you turn to God you will perish for ever. He says: “It is better, being put to death by men, to look for the hope from God of being raised again by him; for you there will be no resurrection to life.” If you, a tyrant, hear from us that you will not attain the resurrection to life if you remain in this unbelief, that you will rise not to rest but to everlasting punishment, what insult is that? Scripture also tells that the fifth, when he had been brought forward and tortured, said to the king: “You have power among men, though you are corruptible; you do what you will. But do not think that our race has been forsaken by God. Wait patiently and see how his great power will torment you and your offspring.” What do you think, given that the servant of God inveighed with such steadfastness against your fellow tyrant? Will you, a worshiper of the devil, judge that worshiper of God to have been insulting? You will deny that he was proud in speaking the truth; nor should you judge me insolent because I tell you that we are not forsaken by God, for whose sake I endure these things, while you, on the contrary, unless you are corrected, will come to nothing along with your corruptible glory. Look also at what the sixth said, and you will find that we resist you, a turbulent storm, with the same battle line with which they resisted: “Do not be deceived in vain; for we suffer these things because of ourselves, having sinned against our God, and they have come about as a fitting chastisement; but do not think that you will go unpunished, since you have tried to fight against God.” The letters of my humble self, and my books, though written in rustic language, prove that I have often said that it was indeed our sins that brought us into your hands, you forerunner of the Antichrist, but that you are fighting against God, and that therefore, unless you look to yourself, you, like that Antiochus, will go to eternal punishment, while the Lord will be merciful to us.

You are aggrieved that we reveal you, and who you are, to those entrusted to us, and that we declare it fitting for you, the shadow of Antichrist, to be trampled underfoot by all the soldiers of Christ. "Who," you say, "have been able to trample me?" Those whom you keep shut up in prison because they confess themselves Christians, whom you strip of their inheritance, drive into exile, torture and kill. This is why you judge us insolent: because we urge all those entrusted to us to trample on the devil's head, and to bring your sacrilegious efforts to nothing by the power of the sufferings inflicted on them for Christ, the only Son of God. Then you must count as insolent that most glorious mother of these seven sons as well, for she saw fit to spur her sons on to defeat Antiochus, your fellow madman, saying: "I do not know how you came into being in my womb. It was not I who gave you breath and life, nor I who knit together the limbs of each of you. It was the Creator of the world, who formed the birth of man and who searches out the origin of all things, and he in his mercy will give you back both breath and life, since you now disregard yourselves for the sake of his laws." The devout mother, loving her sons with courage, did not stop saying this to them until she had seen them all put to death. And we, on the other hand, whom he had foretold by the mouth of the prophet as the future shepherds of his flock, saying, "And I will give you shepherds after my own heart, and they will feed you, feeding you with discipline": ought we to have kept silent, so as not to seem insolent to you, the rabid wolf coming to slaughter God's sheep? A woman so set her sons' hearts on fire with the love of God that through their death by the sword she won victories. And you thought it fitting for us to say to the soldiers of Christ: "Do not take up arms against Constantius, the devil's henchman; do not resist the temple of all the demons; instead do whatever he commands"! What is this defiance of ours, if we strive to fulfil the office God has entrusted to us, if in short we are found to be imitators of this woman? You want to please the devil, whose work you are found carrying out, and you do not at all want us to become most acceptable to God by opposing you while you do these things. If it still troubles you that we call you by these names, hear also what the seventh son of this woman cried out against Antiochus: "But Antiochus, thinking himself despised and scorning the voice of the one who reproached him, since the youngest was still left, not only urged him with words but even swore on oath that he would make him rich and happy, would bring him over from his ancestral ways, would take him as a friend and entrust him with important affairs. But when the youth paid no heed to this, he called the mother and urged her to bring about the youth's safety. And when he had urged her at great length, she undertook to persuade her son. So, leaning toward him, she mocked the cruel tyrant and said in their ancestral tongue: 'My son, have pity on me, who carried you in my womb for ten months, gave you milk for three years, nourished you and brought you up to this age. I beg you, child, to look at heaven and earth, and when you have seen everything in them, to understand that God made them out of nothing, and that the human race comes into being in the same way. Do not fear this executioner, but prove yourself worthy of your brothers and accept death, so that in that mercy he may receive you back together with your brothers.' When she had said this, the youth said: 'Whom are you waiting for? I do not obey the king's command; I obey the precept of the law that was given to us through Moses. But you, who have become the contriver of every evil against the Hebrews, will not escape the hand of God. For if our Lord is angry with us the living for a little while, for the sake of rebuke and correction, he will be reconciled to his servants again. But you, wicked man, most villainous of all men, do not be vainly lifted up, puffed up with empty hopes against his servants; for you have not yet escaped the judgement of almighty God, who sees all things. Our brothers, having now endured a brief pain, have come under God's covenant of eternal life; but you, by the judgement of God, will pay the just penalty for your pride. I, like my brothers, give up both soul and body for our ancestral laws, calling on God to show mercy soon to our nation, and to make you confess under torments and scourges that he alone is God. And in me and in my brothers the wrath of the Almighty, which has justly been brought upon our whole race, will come to a stop.'"

What more, Constantius, have you heard from us than what was said by this faithful servant of God? If he said to the henchmen of Antiochus, "Whom are you waiting for? I do not obey the king's command; I obey the precept of the law that was given to us through Moses," we too say to yours: "Why do you suppose you can make us Arians at the will of Constantius, the forerunner of Antichrist? As we are Christians, so we shall always be." If he said to Antiochus, "But you, who have become the contriver of every evil against the Hebrews, will not escape the hand of God," we too have said to you, and still say, that since there has never been a greater persecutor of God's sacred law than you, you will not escape the hand of God. If Antiochus heard that the Lord was angry with his own people at that time in order to reprove them, and that he would be reconciled to his servants again, you hear us saying the same. If it was said to that king, "But you, wicked man, most villainous of all men, do not be vainly lifted up, puffed up with empty hope against his servants; for you have not yet escaped the judgement of almighty God, who sees all things," you too hear the same from us: that you are wicked, the most villainous of all men, since you do these things in order to make us your fellow apostates; but that you are lifted up in vain, puffed up at the devil's prompting with an empty hope against us, God's servants, since you can neither achieve your malicious designs nor escape the judgement of God, who sees all and can do all. You hear from us, just as Antiochus heard through that illustrious youth, that our brothers, having endured a little, have come under God's covenant of eternal life, while you will pay the just penalty for your pride at the judgement of God. You hear from us too that we are ready to be killed by you, the executioner, for God, just as you have already killed our brothers; that we are ready to give up our souls and bodies for Jesus Christ, the true and only Son of God; and moreover that we trust in his unwearying goodness that he will soon rescue his whole flock from you, the ravening wolf, from you, the rabid dog, while you, unless you look to yourself, will depart into everlasting torment. What more have I said to you, whether in my writings or face to face? I want you to prove it, you tyrant of our time. If I called you an executioner, so did not only this most righteous youth but also his mother, speaking to Antiochus, your fellow madman. If I called you the contriver of every evil, if I said that you will not escape the hand of God, if I called you wicked and the most villainous of all men, because you will not escape the judgement of him who can do all and sees all, but will pay the just penalty at the judgement of God, all of this had already been said by this devout youth to your colleague Antiochus. You keep crying out that I am insulting, because you see names given to you that fit your deeds, the very names that our forerunners, the worshippers of the living God, have already given to your fellow tyrants. The blessed apostle Peter says: "Be sober, be watchful. Your adversary the devil prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour. Resist him, firm in the faith, knowing that your brotherhood throughout the world is enduring these same sufferings." If you think I am insulting because you hear that what you do is evil, how else am I to be found resisting the devil according to the apostle's precept? For look: this dragon, leading you with his wine into utter drunkenness, has let you loose upon the whole flock of God, so that with the help of your royal power you may make everyone drunk as you yourself are, that is, insane, senseless and demented. Has he not made you so drunk from the vine of Sodom and the vineyard of Gomorrah that you do not see that you have committed fornication, just as the Jews committed fornication? How, I ask, shall we resist the devil if no one goes out to oppose you, the one through whom he has armed himself to devour us? How, if the sober do not say to the drunkard, the healthy to the sick, the whole to the wounded, those who see to the blind, those who stand to the fallen, the godly to the ungodly, God's sheep to the ravening wolf, the most kindly lovers of mercy to the cruel executioner and savage murderer, those who glorify God to the blasphemer, the worshippers of God to the sacrilegious, Christians to an Arian [?] heretic, if we do not say to you: "Depart, servant of our adversary; give honour to God"? How shall we resist the devil if we spare you, the dragnet of his will; if your drunkenness, that is, your madness, is not declared to all; if, in short, the very fact that you rage against us does not reveal to the whole world that, doing these things, you cannot be thought a servant of Christ, but plainly the slave of him who is like a roaring lion against us? This is why we seem impudent to you: because we tell you that you have been made drunk with that wine by which those others too were led into all the madness of drunkenness, those to whom, or about whom, it is said: "They have sinned; they are not his children, they are blemished; a crooked and perverse generation. Is this how you repay the Lord? O foolish and unwise people?" And further on: "Jacob drank wine and ate and was filled, and the beloved one kicked; he grew fat and thick and broad, and he abandoned God who made him and departed from God his Saviour. They provoked me with strange gods; with their abominations they stirred me to anger. They sacrificed to demons and not to God, to gods they had not known; new gods have come lately, whom their fathers did not know. You have abandoned the God who begot you, and forgotten the God who nourishes you." Your faithlessness, which you proclaim, proves that you, like the Jews, have abandoned God and followed idolatry.

But for now I thought I should bring you only this far: to see that we are not abusive, impudent and arrogant because I tell you what you are, but truthful, and fearing no one but God. When the most blessed apostle John says, "Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God, for many false prophets have gone out," you plainly seem to me to be one of those false prophets, since by denying the only Son of God you declare that you have nothing but the spirit of Antichrist in your sacrilegious mouth. That is why you cannot even bear to hear us speak of the divine eternity of the only Son of God: the spirit of Antichrist that dwells in you cannot endure it and does not want to be driven out of you, but longs to go on dwelling in you until he sees you carried off to those places where he himself will be for ever. For it grieves him to have you, his most faithful darling, you who obey all his desires, snatched away from him. "Beloved," he says, "do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God, for many false prophets have gone out into the world. By this you recognize the Spirit of God: every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God, and every spirit that destroys Jesus is not from God, and this is the spirit of Antichrist." And further on: "They are of the world; therefore they speak of the world, and the world listens to them. But we are from God. Whoever knows God listens to us; whoever is not from God does not listen to us. By this we recognize the spirit of truth and the spirit of error." It is clear, Constantius, that you carry the spirit of Antichrist and are driven by the spirit of error. For just as those who said that the only Son of God did not take manhood from the womb of the blessed Virgin, who did not believe that he became incarnate and was made man, are shown to have the spirit of error and are called antichrists, so too you Arians: when you deny that the only Son of God was truly born of the Father, that is, of the Father's substance; when you spurn the truth that he is the true Son and has always reigned with the Father; when you refuse to believe that the Son was never without the Father nor the Father without the Son; when you deny that the Father and his only Son have one Godhead, whose spirit do you show yourselves to be full of, if not Antichrist's? No one who has the Spirit of God can say of the only Son of God, "There was a time when he was not, and he was made out of nothing," since he believes that the Son has reigned with the Father without beginning and will reign without end. So when you say that he is not the true Son of God, and when, in short, you try to destroy the truth that he is homoousios [?], as the Greeks say, or, as we Romans say, of one substance with the Father, you surely declare that you too are among those false prophets and antichrists.

You must not judge me insulting because I say that you are driven by an unclean spirit, because I call you the forerunner of Antichrist; for your own mouth reveals that this is what you are. No one who has the Spirit of God could maintain what you Arians assert, you and all your fellow heretics of the various sects. You deny that God has a true Son, you say he is adopted, and you suppose that no one recognizes that you are one of those antichrists whom John declares with his own mouth. You have been exposed, I say, as led by a hostile spirit. That, in the end, is why we did not believe you when you said of the Son, "He was made out of nothing." For we knew that no one could say such things but the spirit of a false prophet, the forerunner of Antichrist, the henchman and slave of demons. We could not believe you when you said this, since the Holy Spirit spoke through the prophets about the only Son of God, that he is the true Son of God, that he is eternal and coeternal with the Father, that the Son was never without the Father, nor was or is the Father without the Son; and the blessed apostles have taught the same, since the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, who was in the prophets, also dwelt in the apostles. And since this Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, is in the Church of God, and you have placed yourselves outside the Church of God, he does not dwell in you, and so you are surely proven to have the spirit of Antichrist. That unclean spirit floods your heretical hearts with darkness, blind with the fog of errors, so that you may not see what we press upon you, and so cannot struggle free of his snares. You judge us insulting because we declare you to be what we see you are. Look: when I find in the Gospel according to Matthew that the Lord said, "Behold, I send you out as sheep among wolves," you seem to me to be one of those wolves, and indeed one in whom I see heaped up the fury of all the wolves that roar against God's flock. For what denier of God's only Son would not rejoice and openly boast when he sees how you have laid waste the flock of Christ? I count you also among those unbelievers, those faithless ones, to whom it is said: "Brood of vipers, how can you speak good things when you are evil? For out of the abundance of the heart each one speaks with his mouth. The good man brings out good things from his good treasure, and the evil man brings out evil things from his evil treasure." If what you say is good, Constantius, then you may have a good treasure. I am impudent because I tell you that darkness dwells in your heart, and that it is from your utterly darkened mind, being what you are, that you dare to bring forth unclean and dark things. Look too: if you hear what the Lord said to blessed Peter, you will no doubt call me insulting. The most holy Matthew says: "While he was still speaking, behold, Judas, one of the Twelve, came, and with him a great crowd with swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests and the elders of the people. Now the betrayer had given them a sign, saying, 'Whomever I kiss, he is the one; seize him.' And at once he went up to Jesus and said, 'Hail, Rabbi,' and kissed him. Jesus said to him, 'Friend, why have you come?' Then they came forward, laid hands on Jesus and seized him. And behold, one of those who were with Jesus stretched out his hand, drew his sword, struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his ear. Then Jesus said to him, 'Put your sword back in its place; for all who take the sword will perish by the sword.'" You will have to call me insulting when you hear that if you use the sword you will perish by the sword. Or have you not used the sword? If you have killed none of the Christians by the sword, if you have persecuted none of them to death because he confessed that God's only Son is the true Son, because he held the apostolic and evangelical faith, because he refused to be an Arian, then perhaps you will be able not to perish by the sword. For you hear what was said to blessed Peter, and said, at that, by God, the only Son of God: that everyone who uses the sword will perish by the sword. Am I insulting because I have told you that Christians are not permitted to kill, since it befits Christians to suffer wrong, not to do it, to be killed; for those who call themselves Christians ought to be killed for Christ, not to kill [?]? These are the commandments the Lord has given us; if we keep them, then we shall continue to be Christians. You, on the other hand, since you see fit to persecute his servants with the sword, we certainly can no longer call a Christian, but plainly a bandit or a gladiator.

Meanwhile, since we have recounted how your fellow madman Judas Iscariot betrayed the Lord, let us here examine thoroughly the causes of his sacrilege and of yours, and you will find that you and Judas Iscariot are one and the same. He handed the Lord over to the Jews because he believed in him only as your fellow Scotinus of Sirmium now believes, the man who was and still is undeservedly called Photinus. You have handed him over, and indeed to the whole world, so that all may deny his divinity. Which of you is the greater in crime? I think you are. For "everyone who sins against the Son of Man will be forgiven; but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, either here or in the world to come." You have made yourself the betrayer of his Godhead, so that all may deny it. For as far as it lies with you, you have betrayed him: you have published written books about him and set up preachers of your "kindly" wishes everywhere. So that all might deny that he is the true Son of God, you had the apostolic and evangelical faith, set down at Nicaea against you heretics, judged heretical, and had your own blasphemy called catholic. And yet this Judas who had betrayed him, seeing that he had brought about the ruin of his own salvation, was moved to repentance and brought the thirty pieces of silver back to the chief priests and elders, saying, "I have sinned in betraying innocent blood." But they said, "What is that to us? See to it yourself." And throwing the silver into the temple, he withdrew, went away and hanged himself. He, though only for a moment, repented and gave back the price he had received. What have you done to match that? Confronted by his servants for committing an outrage, you not only have not repented but have grown still more defiant. What have you done to match that? You pour out all the resources of your realm to strengthen your sacrilege; those you could not corrupt from the truth by any other means, some of them at least you have corrupted with enormous rewards from your wealth; and you have enriched a certain number of the poor so lavishly that they can rival your counts in the size of their fortunes. Judas, once he recognized his crime, ended his life with a noose. You, who for the magnitude of your wickedness deserve a heavier punishment, what will you do when you realize, however late, that you have done evil, when your eyes, festering with heretical poison, begin to see what eyes free of that festering can see now? And yet, if you are willing to believe, what you do out of ignorance must be forgiven you, just as you see it was forgiven the blessed apostle Paul. But if not, you will go down like Judas into the night of hell, and then you will say to those who now drive you to do these things, that is, to your fellow Arians: "I have sinned with you in denying the only Son of God; I have sinned by giving you authority to deny his eternal mercy." Then, when you begin to understand that we rightly confess one eternity of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, when you begin to see that there is one greatness and one power in the Father, in his only Son and in the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, where then will they be who drove you to commit this sacrilege, so that you may say to them: "I repent that I ran with you, God's enemies, that I persecuted the house of God with you"? They will be with you in hell, without a doubt. Where then will the riches of your realm be, which serve not your salvation but your eternal destruction? We do indeed pray that God may see fit to reveal the truth to you, the enemy of your own salvation, and that you may escape from such great dangers. But how far you surpass Judas Iscariot in crime is no labour to judge, since you have summoned the whole world to deny his divinity, whereas Judas handed the Lord over only to those who had not yet believed in him; you, by contrast, have seen fit to incite even those who already believed to deny his Godhead. Judas used force on no one to make them perish with him; you, on the other hand, fight with armed troops against us, whom you know to believe as the patriarchs, prophets, apostles and martyrs believed. Surely it is no great labour to weigh how far apart you and Judas stand.

You call me insulting because I do not want myself, or those entrusted to me, to be wounded by your pestilential doctrine; because I tell you that you are full of disease and must therefore be shunned by the servants of God, so that we do not ourselves become diseased and perish together with you by this plague of yours. "I wish," says the apostle to the Corinthians, "that you would bear with a little of my foolishness; indeed, do bear with me. For I am jealous for you with the jealousy of God. I betrothed you to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin to Christ. But I fear that, as the serpent deceived Eve by his cunning, your minds may be corrupted from the chastity that is in Christ Jesus." That is why I seem insulting to you: because I fear that by your blasphemy you may corrupt the chastity we have in Christ Jesus; because we are afraid that, as your dearest serpent deceived Eve by his cunning, you may lead us away from God and make us liable to death. You think me insolent because I call you a deceitful workman, a false Christian. I am not the first to say these things against you. For you hear that the blessed apostle has marked you out as a deceitful workman, a false apostle: "For such false apostles are deceitful workmen, disguising themselves as apostles of Christ. And no wonder, for Satan himself disguises himself as an angel of light; so it is no great thing if his ministers also disguise themselves as ministers of righteousness. Their end will be according to their deeds." This is why I seem proud to you: because, knowing it from your deeds, I say that you are one of those whom the Holy Spirit foretold through the apostle would be such. If you are not a deceitful workman, refute me; for I know that you pretend to be a Christian although you are an Arian, and that you have wanted to make all of us the servants of him whose henchman you are. If you are not a deceitful workman, prove it; for we see you pretending to be pious in some things while you practise all your impiety against us Christians. If you are not a deceitful workman, how is it that, while pretending to establish peace, you tried to destroy the whole church of God and to dissolve the peace handed down to it through the only Son of God? For I could not have had the Lord's peace from the moment I had done what you were ordering me to do against the Lord's command, from the moment I had at last begun to deny the only Son of God himself, as you deny him. If you have not disguised yourself as the apostles of Christ, why are you so anxious, as though the whole care of the church truly belonged to you—anxious, that is, that no catholic bishop should preside over a church anywhere, that no one should be left who could confess himself a Christian? You remove catholic bishops, you ordain heretics, you write dreadful threats in case sedition should arise. Certainly anyone who does not know, seeing you do these things, supposes you are a Christian; but we, blessedly taught by the apostle, know that Satan has disguised himself as an angel of light—Satan, who carries out all these things against the holy church through you. We cannot be surprised if we see you as his minister, a minister of unrighteousness disguised as a minister of righteousness. We urge you: would that you would turn yourself to this, so that you may be believed a servant of God, so that you may be judged and recognized as a Christian. Whenever we tell you that you could not have become a denier of the only Son of God unless you were full of the adverse spirit, you are in the habit of saying that we do you wrong. And although I have already proved in a great many places that you come against the household of God with unclean spirits inciting your hearts, take further what happened in the Acts of the Apostles: "It happened, as we were going to prayer, that a certain girl who had a spirit of divination met us, who brought her masters much profit by fortune-telling. She followed Paul and us and cried out, saying, 'These men are servants of the Most High God, who proclaim to us the way of salvation.' She did this for many days. Paul was grieved, and turning to the spirit he said, 'I command you in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her.' And it came out that very hour. But when her masters saw that their hope of profit had gone out, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them into the marketplace before the magistrates, and brought them forward, saying, 'These men are throwing our city into confusion, being Jews, and they proclaim a sect which it is not lawful for us to accept or practise, since we are Romans.' And the whole crowd rose up together against them, and the magistrates tore off their tunics and ordered them to be beaten with rods. When they had laid many blows on them, they threw them into prison, ordering the jailer to keep them securely. Having received such an order, he put them in the innermost part of the prison and fastened their feet in the stocks. About midnight, as Paul and Silas were praying and singing a hymn to God, the other prisoners were listening to them. Suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken; the doors were opened, and all the bonds were loosed. The jailer woke up, and when he saw the prison doors open, he drew his sword to kill himself, thinking that the prisoners had escaped. But Paul cried out with a loud voice, saying, 'Do yourself no harm, for we are all here.' Hearing this, the jailer called for a light and went in, and trembling he fell down at the feet of Paul and Silas; and when he had brought them outside, he said, 'Sirs, what must I do to be saved?' And they said, 'Believe in God Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household.' And they spoke the word of the Lord to him and to all who were in his house. And taking them that very hour of the night, he washed their wounds, and he was baptized, he and all his household. Then he brought them into his house and set a table before them, and he feasted with all his household, believing in the Lord."

So then, just as that spirit of divination, on hearing the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, was immediately driven out of its dwelling and stirred up the whole people of the city against the preachers of the majesty of the only Son of God, so those unclean spirits have stirred up you and your people against us, his servants. And do not doubt that you are driven by the same spirits that drove those who rose up against Paul and Silas, since you see yourself made in this way a persecutor of God's religion. That mob had not yet believed in the only Son of God, and it was what it was for no other reason than that it was without the Spirit of God—as you too are shown to be. For that you cannot have the Holy Spirit unless you believe in the only Son of God is made plain by what that jailer did. Although he was certainly one of that resisting people, yet after he believed, because he was now governed by the Holy Spirit by whom Paul and Silas were governed, he embraced nothing but the way of those for whose sake he had seen the prison doors opened of their own accord. So you, who are now driven by a contrary spirit, unless you believe in the only Son of God as we too believe, can have in you nothing but the spirit of our adversary. For that jailer said to the glorious Paul and Silas, "Sirs, what must I do to be saved?" And they said, "Believe in our Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household." It is clear, then, that you are not saved, because you have not yet believed in the Lord Jesus. Nor can you claim to have believed in him, since you persecute him. Or do you imagine that you are not persecuting him himself in us? If you are not persecuting him in us, how is it that he himself says to Saul: "Why are you persecuting me? I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting. It is hard for you to kick against the goad"? What was Saul doing, to hear these words from the Lord? Exactly what you are doing; for he denied the only Son of God just as you deny him. For Paul—then a persecutor, but afterwards one who himself began to suffer persecution—did not persecute the Christians because they believed as you believe, that there was a time when he was not, that he was made from nothing, and that he is [?] a true Son; but surely because they dared to confess the only Son of God, because the Christians declared that they believed that the eternity of the Father and the Son is one, that the deity is one, that the power in the Father and the Son is one. Paul abhorred these things, thinking the Christians were in error; but when he was enlightened by the one he was denying, when he came to understand from the books of Moses and from all the volumes of the prophets, he at once began to defend what he had been attacking—namely, what those he persecuted had defended before he believed. Otherwise, who was ever so senseless—as you Arians are, or as Photinus of Sirmium is, who is more truly called Scotinus—as to believe in a creature, in one of whom there was a time when he was not, in one who was created from nothing? It is evident, then, that all of you, who do not believe as the glorious church believes, are led by the adverse spirit; and from that adverse spirit you cannot be freed unless you believe that he is the true Son of God.

"The bishops," you say, "insult me." Why do we seem insulting to you? Surely because we say: Why do you pretend to be a Christian? For you are plainly an Arian, plainly an enemy of God's religion. That is why we seem injurious to you and yours. But consider what the most blessed apostle said, so that we bishops might act against you wolves: "You know, from the first day that I set foot in Asia, how I was with you the whole time, serving the Lord with all humility and tears and the trials that befell me through the plots of the Jews; how I held back nothing that was profitable, how I proclaimed to you and taught you publicly and from house to house, testifying to Jews and Greeks of repentance toward God and faith in our Lord Jesus. And now, behold, bound in the Spirit, I am going to Jerusalem, not knowing what will befall me there, except that the Holy Spirit testifies to me in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions await me in Jerusalem. But I count my life of no value to me, provided I may finish my course and the ministry of the word which I received from the Lord, to testify to Jews and Greeks the gospel of the grace of God. And now I know that none of you, among whom I have gone about preaching the kingdom of the Lord Jesus, will see my face again. Therefore I testify to you this day that I am clean of the blood of all, for I have not held back from proclaiming the whole will of God. Take heed to yourselves and to all the flock, in which the Holy Spirit has made you bishops, to rule the church of the Lord, which he obtained with his own blood. I know that after my departure fierce wolves will come in among you, not sparing the flock; and from among yourselves men will arise speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them. Therefore be watchful, remembering that for three years I did not cease night and day to warn each one of you with tears." Since you see that these are the apostle's commands, what do you order me to do, so as not to seem insulting to you? Surely you order me to keep silent and let you, as one of those fierce wolves foretold, rage against God's flock however you please. We see you wolves, whom the Holy Spirit deigned to foretell through the apostle, the chosen vessel, trying to seize the whole flock of God; and are we, the bishops whom the Holy Spirit has appointed to rule the church of God, as the blessed apostle says, to spare you, a wolf? Are we to revere the diadem of your kingdom, your earrings too and your armlets? Are we to honor your garments, which you consider so distinguished, and despise the Creator and Ruler of all things? Who is more foolish than you, to say, "I, the emperor, suffer insult from Lucifer, a pauper"?—not even deigning to say "from a bishop," because you have been recognized as a wolf and have deserved to be rebuffed. You thought I should be loaded with such odium that you could claim a servant of God had been insulting to you, the emperor. If you think us insulting, hear what the blessed Paul answered the chief priest who forbade him to preach the only Son of God. "Paul, looking intently at the council," says Scripture, "said, 'Brothers, I have lived before God in all good conscience up to this day.' And the high priest Ananias commanded those standing by him to strike Paul on the mouth. Then Paul said to him, 'God will strike you, you whitewashed wall! Do you sit to judge me according to the law, and yet, contrary to the law, order me to be struck?'" So if the sacred law cannot judge the blessed Paul insulting because he said this to an unjust judge, neither can you justly call me proud when I tell you the truth and what you are. You brand me guilty of insults; but tell me, I beg you, to whom can you complain about me? If to God, how can you complain to one you do not know? How, when you are a stranger to his house? But if you complain to yourself, what will you, a mere man, do, when you can in no way harm the servants of God? If you torture us, we are the more healed; if you torment us, we are the more refreshed; if you kill us, we shall live the more.

You call me injurious because I dare to call you the forerunner of Antichrist. If your own deeds do not show you to be this, then consider with great care the book of the most holy prophet Daniel too, and you will find yourself to be one of those persecutors of God's religion foretold there. "In the first year of Belshazzar, king of the Chaldeans, Daniel saw a dream, and visions of his head upon his bed, and he wrote down his dream: I, Daniel, was watching; and behold, the four winds of heaven were rushing upon the great sea, and four beasts came up out of the sea, each surpassing the other in size. The first was like a lioness, and had wings. And it rose up from the earth and stood on the feet of a man, and the heart of a man was given to it. And behold, another beast, like a she-bear, and it stood on one side, and there were three ribs in its mouth, between its teeth; and they said to it thus: Arise, devour much flesh. After this beast I looked, and behold, another beast like a leopard, and it had four wings of a bird upon it, and the beast had four heads, and dominion was given to it. After this I looked, and behold, a fourth beast, terrible and astonishing and exceedingly strong; its iron teeth devoured and broke in pieces, and it trampled the rest with its feet. And this beast was greater than the other beasts that had been seen before, and it had ten horns. And I was considering its horns, and behold, another, smaller horn came up among them, and three of the horns that were before it were uprooted before it. And behold, in this horn were eyes like the eyes of a man, and a mouth speaking great things. I watched until thrones were set in place, and the Ancient of Days sat. His clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool; his throne was a flame of fire, its wheels burning fire. A river of fire shone before him; thousands of thousands served him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him. He sat in judgment, and the books were opened. I watched then because of the sound of the great words which that horn was speaking, until the beast was destroyed and perished, and its body was given over to be burned. And the dominion of the rest of the beasts was taken away, and a length of life was given them for a time [?]. I saw in the vision of the night, and behold, with the clouds of heaven one like a son of man was coming, and he came to the Ancient of Days; he came before him and was presented to him, and to him was given dominion and honor and kingdom, and all peoples, tribes, and tongues serve him. His power is an everlasting power that will never pass away, and his kingdom [?] will be destroyed. My spirit shuddered within me, I, Daniel, and the visions of my head troubled me. And I approached one of those standing by and sought from him the truth about all these things. And he told me the truth and made known to me the interpretation of the words: These four great beasts are four kingdoms that will arise on the earth; and the saints of the Most High God will receive the kingdom and possess it for ever. And I inquired diligently about the fourth beast, which was different from all the other beasts and exceedingly terrible; its teeth were of iron and its claws of bronze; it devoured and broke in pieces and trampled the rest with its feet; and about its ten horns, which were on its head, and about the other horn which came up and shook out the first three horns, the horn that had eyes and a mouth speaking great things, and whose appearance was greater than the rest. I watched, and that horn made war with the saints and prevailed against them, until the Ancient of Days came and gave judgment for the saints of the Most High God; and the time arrived, and the saints possessed the kingdom. And he said: The fourth beast will be a fourth kingdom on earth, which will surpass all kingdoms, and it will devour the whole earth and trample it and break it in pieces. As for its ten horns, ten kings will arise, and after them another will arise who will surpass in evil all who were before him; and he will bring low three kings, and he will speak words against the Most High God, and will wear out the saints of the Most High God, and will think to change times and law; and they will be given into his hand for a time, times, and half a time. And the judgment will sit, and his dominion will be taken away, to be consumed and destroyed to the end; and the kingdom and the power and the greatness of the kings will be given to the saints of the Most High God. And his kingdom is everlasting, and all will serve and obey him."

I ought, indeed, to have quoted only the part that shows, through your deeds, which of the beasts you resemble. But so that you might know that you will be in that Gehenna into which the glorious Daniel reports that the beast was cast, unless you mend your ways, and so that you might notice how those you persecute will reign forever, set in the kingdom of the Lord, we have added all of this. I also judged that the whole revelation should be applied for this purpose: so that, at least by reading it, you might satisfy yourself that you tyrants, persecutors of God's religion, have been called beasts. For I want to clear myself before your conscience, infected with the poisons of the Arian dogma—before you, who are not a religious man but a destroyer of religion—and to show that I am not, as you claim, insulting because I call you a wild beast or a savage monster, since you see that this is what you are called, names having been applied to you according to your deeds. Moreover, it is plain that you bear the likeness of that fourth beast, and that you are eager to fulfill what it was foretold that beast would fulfill. It is written of the Antichrist, whom you resemble, or whom you are judged to be yourself: "He will speak words against the Most High [?], and will wear out the saints of the Most High God, and will think to change times and law, and it will be given into his hand." These things you have already done and are still doing. For when you say, "The Son of God is not true God, but was made from nothing," you speak words against God. For since we Christians claim one divinity for the Father and his only Son, and you attack this defense of ours, asserting of the Son that there was a time when he was not and that he was made from nothing, you surely prove that you are either the Antichrist or at least his forerunner. Indeed, you cannot be understood to be anything other than either the forerunner of Antichrist or Antichrist himself, since you dare to call the apostolic and evangelical faith heretical and try to claim your blasphemy as the catholic faith. You feel that you are wronged because we call you a beast; yet you are found thinking to change the faith, that is, so that we should not believe as the patriarchs, prophets, apostles, and martyrs believed, but you have decreed that we must believe as your fellow-reprobate Arius did. And do you say you are not rightly called a beast, when the most holy prophet called you a beast because you would do these things? You are not less than Antichrist in unbelief, Constantius; for you never cease devouring the servants of God with iron teeth. Why say more? Antichrist will do nothing but bring about the denial of the only Son of God; and this is exactly what your most unclean mind, fattened on folly, is doing.

But however much you rage, your times will pass, they will pass, and those times will come when, unless you look to your own good, you will see yourself set in that river of fire. Then you will see those whom you so savagely persecute, because they refuse to perish with you, not in that place of torment where you will be, but with the holy angels, forever giving thanks and praise to God, while you are in that liquid flame. I do not want you to wonder that the glorious Daniel marked you out as a beast, since the blessed Paul too said of your fellows, the Cretans: “Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, lazy bellies”; and further on: “Therefore rebuke them sharply, so that they may be sound in the faith, not paying heed to Jewish fables and to the commandments of men who turn away from the truth.” This is why we bishops seem insulting to you: because we rebuke and reprove you, asking why you dared to turn away from the truth, why you chose to abandon God's commandments and cling to the blasphemies and commandments of men, why, in short, you abandoned God and took up idolatry. This is why I seem to be your enemy: because I want you to walk according to the apostle's precept and not according to the commandments of Arius and the Jews. Against these most just charges of ours, seeing yourself overcome by the truth, you are accustomed to say: “The sacred Scriptures command that you must be subject to kings and to all who are in high places, and you dare to heap so many such things on me, Lucifer?” These passages you notice; passages of this kind, which order that you be honored, you understand. But those that order what you must do you pretend not to know: those that warn you to obey the priests of the Lord, those that insist that you must show yourself as one among all your fellow servants and must not call yourself superior to anyone, if you wish to be found a servant of God. “Speak these things,” says the blessed apostle to Titus, “and exhort and rebuke with all authority; let no one despise you.” If you are a Christian, since you too are one of those on whose account he said, “Speak these things and exhort and rebuke with all authority; let no one despise you,” then you certainly ought to listen to me when I correct you with all authority, and not despise me. You will be a Christian if you do not despise me when I urge you to remain a Christian; but if you do despise me, you are found to be no longer among the Christians, because if you had been a Christian, you would not have despised the one whom God appointed to instruct his people, the one to whom the apostle said, “Speak these things and exhort and rebuke with all authority; let no one despise you.” For what am I urging on you? Only that you not be a murderer, that you not persecute the house of God, that you stop torturing, proscribing, deporting, shutting up in prison, butchering, destroying in various ways and killing those you see to be Christians; that you stop, finally, blaspheming the only Son of God; that you accept the apostolic faith, which you call heretical—this faith of ours, namely, which the bishops set down at Nicaea against you and all the heretics; that you believe as we do and deign to reject the idolatry instituted by Arius your master, so that you may proclaim yourself a Christian, not an Arian; that you stop bringing false charges against the priests of God. This is my correction, this my reproof. The apostle tells me to rebuke you with all authority, and you say, “Lucifer is insulting me,” and do not say, “A priest of God is admonishing and exhorting me according to the precepts given to priests, so that I may lead a life most acceptable to God.”

As for your saying that we owe you obedience, know that we recognize ourselves bound to render obedience not to you alone but to all who are in high places. For the apostle says: “Remind them to be subject to princes and magistrates, to be obedient, ready for every good work, to blaspheme no one, not to be quarrelsome but gentle, showing all meekness toward all people. For we too were once foolish and unbelieving, going astray, enslaved to various desires and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, hating one another. But when the kindness and love for humankind of God our Savior shone forth, he saved us, not because of works of righteousness that we had done, but according to his mercy, through the washing of regeneration and renewal through the Holy Spirit, whom he poured out on us richly through Jesus Christ our Savior, so that, justified by his grace, we might become heirs according to the hope of life.” He reminds us, then, that we must be subject in good works, not in evil ones. If it is a good work to destroy a man in his absence, to put to death without a hearing one who cries out that he wishes to clear himself, to cast aside all regard for mercy and join you in punishing one we know to be innocent; if it is a good work to deny the only Son of God, if it is a work acceptable to God to desert the apostolic faith and embrace the heretical one, then you would rightly say that I act against the admonitions of the sacred Scriptures. I add this too: the apostle made mention of those princes and magistrates who had not yet believed in the only Son of God, so that they might be drawn to belief by our humility and meekness, by our long patience in adversity, and by our utmost obedience in fitting matters. But if you, because you are emperor, pretending to be one of us, compel us to abandon God and take up idolatry, must we really give in to you, lest the apostle's precepts appear to have been neglected? And yet you, who pretend to be a Christian, try to make Christians what you yourself are, that is, apostates—you who are still foolish and unbelieving, persisting in your malice, in which the apostle says we too once were, before we came to knowledge, before we received the holy faith. In what were we to accommodate you, except by carrying out what was lawful? Or when you say, you blasphemous murderer, “Kill those who believe in the only Son of God; be persecutors of his house with me; deny him with me; reject the apostolic faith; embrace my heresy, of which I have been a lover with all the strength of my heart,” who would be more wretched than you if he did not shun you, did not flee from you, recognizing that you who urge such things are a temple of demons? Because you hear these things, you say, “I suffer insult from Lucifer, a wretched man, and I an emperor at that!” And that blasphemous, defiled speech of yours does not go on to say, “I hear what I deserve from Lucifer, a priest of the Lord.”

The vessel of election says to the Galatians: “I marvel that you are so quickly being transferred from him who called you in grace to another gospel, which is not another; except that there are some who trouble you and want to pervert the gospel of Christ. But even if we or an angel from heaven should preach to you anything other than the gospel, let him be anathema. As we have said before, so now I say again: if anyone has proclaimed to you anything other than what you received, let him be anathema.” And do you suppose that I can declare you to be anything other than anathema, when I find you preaching otherwise than the blessed apostles handed down? So when you hear from me that I hold you anathema for preaching otherwise than the apostles preached, if you call me insulting, you will be able to recognize that you are lying—if you carry anything of a human being in you—since you see that I call you anathema for this reason: that the blessed apostle has already anathematized you. You declare me insulting because I call you a fool; but how can I rightly be called insulting by you, when it is clear that I am speaking the truth—that you are indeed a fool? For if the Galatians hear “O foolish Galatians” from the blessed apostle, why should you think you ought not to be called by the name of fool? For if they were called foolish because they had obeyed false brethren—because, heeding the suggestions of those fellow serpents of yours, they had decided that they must keep the sabbaths and observe circumcision—how much more deservedly are you called a fool, who have shown yourself a denier of the only Son of God! Because I say to you, “Rescue yourself from the rabid Arian dogs; grieve that by clinging to their wicked council you yourself have become a dog,” you call me insolent. But perhaps you do not know that the deniers of the only Son of God have been called dogs, called fat bulls, called sons of iniquity, an adulterous seed and the offspring of a harlot, sons of perdition and a wicked seed. If it has escaped you that you have been so named by God, hear him saying through Isaiah to your fellow blasphemers the Jews: “Come here, you sons of iniquity, adulterous seed and offspring of a harlot. In whom have you taken delight, and against whom have you opened your mouth, and against whom have you let loose your tongue? Are you not sons of perdition, a wicked seed?” And in another place: “See, all have been blinded; they have not known how to understand; all are dumb dogs that will not be able to bark, dreaming in their beds, loving to slumber. And they are shameless dogs, with souls that know no satiety, and they are wicked, without understanding; they have all followed their own ways.” Who are these to whom, or on whose account, these things are said? Surely those whom the only Son of God accuses in the twenty-first Psalm, speaking through the mouth of David: “Many calves have surrounded me, fat bulls have besieged me. They have opened their mouth against me like a lion ravening and roaring”; and further on: “Many dogs have surrounded me, a council of evildoers has besieged me [?]; they have pierced my hands and feet.” So when you notice that those masters of yours in sacrilege were called calves, fat bulls and dogs, you, one of the council of evildoers, cannot judge me insulting for calling you by the names by which your fellow plagues were and are called. For you are no less in wickedness—you who dare to say, “There was a time when he was not, and he was made from nothing”—that you should not be called by those names that fit you. But if you do not want to be called by these names, change your ways, correct your errors, as the most blessed Paul and others from that faithless people corrected theirs. Because I say to you, “Rescue yourself from the council of evildoers,” I seem insulting to you. On what account? Clearly because I profess myself a Christian, because I have refused to abandon God and go after your idolatry. We are not the first to be called insulting and proud by you sacrilegious men; for all those too were so called who resisted the deadly edicts of your fellow tyrants.

To pass over the others as I close my discourse, I will turn once more to King Antiochus alone. Did he judge those who resisted him to be insulting and proud, or not? Without doubt he did; because he thought them insulting and proud, he persecuted those devoted to God with such cruelty, even to death. It remains, then, for you to see what else Antiochus did beyond what you already know; and if you can rightly say that they were proud and insulting toward Antiochus, you can say it of us as well. For we suffer from you what they suffered from Antiochus; we cry out for the faith and for religion just as they cried out; we profess to serve the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, the God of Jacob, just as they confessed. “The king,” says Scripture, “sent an old man of Athens to compel the Jews to depart from the laws of their fathers and of God, so that they should not live by them, and also to defile the temple in Jerusalem and to name it after Olympian Jupiter, and the one in Gerizim, as befitted those who inhabited the place, after Jupiter the Hospitable. The onslaught of these evils was very bad and grievous to all. For the temple was full of the revels of the Gentiles, who were whoring with harlots and approaching women within the sacred precincts, and moreover were bringing in things that were not fitting; the altar too was full of unlawful things forbidden by the laws. Neither were the sabbaths kept nor the ancestral feast days observed.” And further on: “They were led by bitter compulsion every month on the king's birthday; it was a pitiable thing. And when the rites of Liber were celebrated, they were forced to go in procession for Liber wearing ivy. A decree went out to the neighboring Greek cities, at the suggestion of the Ptolemies, that they should take the same course against the Jews and [?], and kill those who would not go over to the customs of the Greeks. One could see, then, the misery. For two women were brought up for having circumcised their sons; they hung the infants at their breasts, led the women publicly around the city, and threw them down from the wall. Others, who had gathered in nearby caves to keep the seventh day in secret, were burned when this was reported, because they were afraid to defend themselves on the glorious holy day.” What do you think the worshipers of God ought to have done then? Ought they to have pleased God or Antiochus? If you think they ought not to have pleased Antiochus, then neither, surely, ought we to please you; for you too, though in a different way, still want to take us away from God and join us to the devil, just as he wanted to do to them. The very same cruelty is carried out by you; so savage and unjust are you toward those who resist your deadly edict. It remains, then, as has often been said, that you grieve over having gone astray, and, recognizing that you are a murderer and a blasphemer, you, deserter of God, restore yourself to his house. Otherwise you will have only yourself to blame when you begin to see yourself there where all those fellow tyrants of yours now are.
